constructible sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules. Then
$$
\epsilon^{-1} :
D_c^+(X_\etale, \Lambda)
\longrightarrow
D_c^+(X_\proetale, \Lambda)
$$
is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.title: Tensor c
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BQ}}


Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $K, L \in D_c^-(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$. Then
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} L$ is in $D_c^-(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$.

nodes.title: Compare truncations constructible
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BR}}


Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring.
Let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$.
Set $K_n = K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I^n}$.
If $K_1$ is in $D^-_c(X_\proetale, \Lambda/I)$, then
$K_n$ is in $D^-_c(X_\proetale, \Lambda/I^n)$ for all $n$.

nodes.title: Adic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BT}}


Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules
on $X_\proetale$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We say $\mathcal{F}$ is a {\it constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf}
if $\mathcal{F} = \lim \mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F}$ and each
$\mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F}$ is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda/I^n$-modules.
\item If $\mathcal{F}$ is a constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf, then we say
$\mathcal{F}$ is {\it lisse} if each $\mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F}$ is
locally constant.
\item We say $\mathcal{F}$ is {\it adic lisse}\footnote{This may
be nonstandard notation.} if there exists a
$I$-adically complete $\Lambda$-module $M$ with $M/IM$ finite
such that $\mathcal{F}$ is locally isomorphic to
$$
\underline{M}^\wedge = \lim \underline{M/I^nM}.
$$
\item We say $\mathcal{F}$ is
{\it adic constructible}\footnote{This may be nonstandard notation.}
if for every affine open $U \subset X$
there exists a decomposition $U = \coprod U_i$ into
constructible locally closed subschemes such that $\mathcal{F}|_{U_i}$
is adic lisse.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Noetherian constructible
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BU}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_\proetale$.
Then there exists a finite partition $X = \coprod X_i$ by
locally closed subschemes such that the restriction $\mathcal{F}|_{X_i}$
is lisse.

nodes.title: Weird
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BV}}


Let $X$ be a weakly contractible affine scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian
ring and $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $X_\proetale$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{F} = \lim \mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F}$,
\item $\mathcal{F}/I^n\mathcal{F}$ is a constant sheaf of
$\Lambda/I^n$-modules,
\item $\mathcal{F}/I\mathcal{F}$ is of finite type.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{F} \cong \underline{M}^\wedge$ where $M$ is
a finite $\Lambda^\wedge$-module.

nodes.title: Connected lisse
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BW}}


Let $X$ be a connected scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let
$I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. If $\mathcal{F}$ is a lisse
constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_\proetale$, then $\mathcal{F}$
is adic lisse.

nodes.title: Noetherian adic constructible
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BX}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_\proetale$. Then $\mathcal{F}$
is adic constructible.

nodes.title: Derived complete zero
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BY}}


Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a ring and let
$I \subset \Lambda$ be a finitely generated ideal.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_\proetale$.
If $\mathcal{F}$ is derived complete and $\mathcal{F}/I\mathcal{F} = 0$,
then $\mathcal{F} = 0$.

nodes.title: Derived complete limit
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09BZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09BZ}}


Let $X$ be a weakly contractible affine scheme.
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a derived complete sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules
on $X_\proetale$ with $\mathcal{F}/I\mathcal{F}$ a locally
constant sheaf of $\Lambda/I$-modules of finite type.
Then there exists an integer $t$ and a surjective map
$$
(\underline{\Lambda}^\wedge)^{\oplus t} \to \mathcal{F}
$$

nodes.title: Dbc
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C1}}


Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal.
Let $X$ be a scheme. An object $K$ of $D(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$ is called
{\it constructible} if
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K$ is derived complete with respect to $I$,
\item $K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I}$
has constructible cohomology sheaves and locally has finite tor dimension.
\end{enumerate}
We denote $D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$ the full subcategory of constructible
$K$ in $D(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$.

nodes.title: Describe constructible complexes
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C2}}


In the situation above suppose $K$ is in $D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$
and $X$ is quasi-compact. Set
$K_n = K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I^n}$.
There exist $a, b$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K = R\lim K_n$ and $H^i(K) = 0$ for $i \not \in [a, b]$,
\item each $K_n$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
\item each $K_n$ has constructible cohomology sheaves,
\item each $K_n = \epsilon^{-1}L_n$ for some
$L_n \in D_{ctf}(X_\etale, \Lambda/I^n)$
(\'Etale Cohomology, Definition \ref{etale-cohomology-definition-ctf}).
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Local structure constructible complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C3}}


Let $X$ be a weakly contractible affine scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian
ring and let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of
$D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$ such that the cohomology sheaves of
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I}$ are locally
constant. Then there exists a finite disjoint open covering
$X = \coprod U_i$ and for each $i$ a finite collection of
finite projective $\Lambda^\wedge$-modules $M^a, \ldots, M^b$
such that $K|_{U_i}$ is represented by a complex
$$
(\underline{M^a})^\wedge \to \ldots \to (\underline{M^b})^\wedge
$$
in $D(U_{i, \proetale}, \Lambda)$ for some maps of sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules $(\underline{M^i})^\wedge \to (\underline{M^{i + 1}})^\wedge$.

nodes.title: Adic constructible
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C4}}


Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let
$I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K \in D(X_\proetale, \Lambda)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We say $K$ is {\it adic lisse}\footnote{This may be
nonstandard notation} if there exists a finite complex of finite
projective $\Lambda^\wedge$-modules $M^\bullet$ such that
$K$ is locally isomorphic to
$$
\underline{M^a}^\wedge \to \ldots \to \underline{M^b}^\wedge
$$
\item We say $K$ is {\it adic constructible}\footnote{This may be
nonstandard notation.} if for every affine open $U \subset X$
there exists a decomposition $U = \coprod U_i$ into
constructible locally closed subschemes such that $K|_{U_i}$
is adic lisse.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Weakly contractible locally constant ML
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C5}}


Let $X$ be a weakly contractible affine scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian
ring and let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of
$D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$ such that
$K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I^n}$
is isomorphic in $D(X_\proetale, \Lambda/I^n)$ to a
complex of constant sheaves of $\Lambda/I^n$-modules. Then
$$
H^0(X, K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \Lambda/I^n)
$$
has the Mittag-Leffler condition.

nodes.title: Connected adic lisse
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C6}}



Let $X$ be a connected scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let
$I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. If $K$ is in $D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$
such that $K \otimes_\Lambda \underline{\Lambda/I}$
has locally constant cohomology sheaves, then $K$ is adic lisse
(Definition \ref{proetale-definition-adic-constructible}).

nodes.title: Noetherian adic constructible
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C7}}



Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and
let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal. Let $K$ be an object of
$D_{cons}(X, \Lambda)$. Then $K$ is adic constructible
(Definition \ref{proetale-definition-adic-constructible}).

nodes.title: Proper base change
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 09C9}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes. Let $g : Y' \to Y$ be
a morphism of schemes giving rise to the base change diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}X' \underset{g'}{\longrightarrow}\underset{f'}{\downarrow} & X \overset{f}{\downarrow} \\ Y' \overset{g}{\longrightarrow} & Y\end{array}
$$
Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I \subset \Lambda$ be an ideal
such that $\Lambda/I$ is torsion. Let $K$ be an object
of $D(X_\proetale)$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K$ is derived complete, and
\item $K \otimes_\Lambda^\mathbf{L} \underline{\Lambda/I^n}$ is
bounded below with cohomology sheaves coming from $X_\etale$,
\item $\Lambda/I^n$ is a perfect $\Lambda$-module\footnote{This assumption
can be removed if $K$ is a constructible complex, see \cite{BS}.}.
\end{enumerate}
Then the base change map
$$
Lg_{comp}^*Rf_*K \longrightarrow Rf'_*L(g')^*_{comp}K
$$
is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Proetale induced
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098J}{\texttt{Stacks tag 098J}}



Let $\Sch_\proetale$ be a big pro-\'etale site as in
Definition \ref{proetale-definition-big-proetale-site}.
Let $T \in \Ob(\Sch_\proetale)$.
Let $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ be an arbitrary pro-\'etale covering of $T$.
There exists a covering $\{U_j \to T\}_{j \in J}$ of $T$ in the site
$\Sch_\proetale$ which refines $\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$.

nodes.title: Proetale cohomology independent partial universe
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098Y}{\texttt{Stacks tag 098Y}}



Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $S_\proetale \subset S_\proetale'$ be
two small pro-\'etale sites of $S$ as constructed in
Definition \ref{proetale-definition-big-small-proetale}. Then the inclusion functor
satisfies the assumptions of
Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-bigger-site}.
Hence there exist morphisms of topoi
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}\Sh(S_\proetale) \overset{g}{\longrightarrow} & \Sh(S_\proetale') \overset{f}{\longrightarrow} & \Sh(S_\proetale)\end{array}
$$
whose composition is isomorphic to the identity and with $f_* = g^{-1}$.
Moreover,
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $\mathcal{F}' \in \textit{Ab}(S_\proetale')$ we have
$H^p(S_\proetale', \mathcal{F}') = H^p(S_\proetale, g^{-1}\mathcal{F}')$,
\item for $\mathcal{F} \in \textit{Ab}(S_\proetale)$ we have
$$
H^p(S_\proetale, \mathcal{F}) =
H^p(S_\proetale', g_*\mathcal{F}) =
H^p(S_\proetale', f^{-1}\mathcal{F}).
$$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Change alpha
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F4S}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0F4S}}



Suppose given big sites $\Sch_\proetale$ and $\Sch'_\proetale$ as in
Definition \ref{proetale-definition-big-proetale-site}.
Assume that $\Sch_\proetale$ is contained in $\Sch'_\proetale$.
The inclusion functor $\Sch_\proetale \to \Sch'_\proetale$ satisfies
the assumptions of Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-bigger-site}.
There are morphisms of topoi
\begin{eqnarray*}
g : \Sh(\Sch_\proetale) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh(\Sch'_\proetale) \\
f : \Sh(\Sch'_\proetale) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh(\Sch_\proetale)
\end{eqnarray*}
such that $f \circ g \cong \text{id}$. For any object $S$
of $\Sch_\proetale$ the inclusion functor
$(\Sch/S)_\proetale \to (\Sch'/S)_\proetale$ satisfies
the assumptions of Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-bigger-site}
also. Hence similarly we obtain morphisms
\begin{eqnarray*}
g : \Sh((\Sch/S)_\proetale) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh((\Sch'/S)_\proetale) \\
f : \Sh((\Sch'/S)_\proetale) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh((\Sch/S)_\proetale)
\end{eqnarray*}
with $f \circ g \cong \text{id}$.

nodes.title: Cohomology enlarge partial universe
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F4T}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0F4T}}



Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $(\Sch/S)_\proetale$ and $(\Sch'/S)_\proetale$ be two
big pro-\'etale sites of $S$ as in
Definition \ref{proetale-definition-big-small-proetale}.
Assume that the first is contained in
the second. In this case
\begin{enumerate}
\item for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}'$ defined on $(\Sch'/S)_\proetale$
and any object $U$ of $(\Sch/S)_\proetale$ we have
$$
H^p(U, \mathcal{F}'|_{(\Sch/S)_\proetale}) =
H^p(U, \mathcal{F}')
$$
In words: the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}'$ over $U$ computed in the bigger site
agrees with the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}'$ restricted to the smaller site
over $U$.
\item for any abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $(\Sch/S)_\proetale$ there is an
abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}'$ on $(\Sch/S)_\proetale'$ whose restriction to
$(\Sch/S)_\proetale$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{F}$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Multiplicities field extension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4F}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4F}}


Let $K/k$ be a field extension. Let $Z$ be an integral locally algebraic
scheme over $k$. The multiplicity $m_{Z', Z_K}$ of an irreducible
component $Z' \subset Z_K$ is $1$ or a power of the characteristic of $k$.

nodes.title: How different
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4G}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4G}}


Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$ with perfect closure $k^{perf}$.
Let $X$ be an algebraic scheme over $k$. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer.
The cokernel of the injective map $Z_r(X) \to Z_r(X_{k^{perf}})$ is a
$p$-power torsion module (More on Algebra, Definition
\ref{more-algebra-definition-f-power-torsion}).

nodes.title: Specialization module
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4I}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4I}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field
$\kappa$. Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $R$. Let $r \geq 0$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module flat over $R$. Assume
$\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}_K)) \leq r$. Then
$\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}_\kappa)) \leq r$ and
$$
sp_{X/R}([\mathcal{F}_K]_r) = [\mathcal{F}_\kappa]_r
$$

nodes.title: Specialization closed
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4J}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4J}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field
$\kappa$. Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $R$. Let $r \geq 0$.
Let $W \subset X$ be a closed subscheme flat over $R$. Assume
$\dim(W_K) \leq r$. Then $\dim(W_\kappa) \leq r$ and
$$
sp_{X/R}([W_K]_r) = [W_\kappa]_r
$$

nodes.title: Specialization extension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4K}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4K}}


Let $R'/R$ be an extension of discrete valuation rings inducing fraction field
extension $K'/K$ and residue field extension $\kappa'/\kappa$
(More on Algebra, Definition
\ref{more-algebra-definition-extension-discrete-valuation-rings}).
Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $R$. Denote $X' = X_{R'}$.
Then the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}Z_r(X'_{K'}) \underset{sp_{X'/R'}}{\longrightarrow} &  & Z_r(X'_{\kappa'}) \\ Z_r(X_K) \overset{sp_{X/R}}{\longrightarrow}\uparrow &  & Z_r(X_\kappa) \uparrow\end{array}
$$
commutes where $r \geq 0$ and the vertical arrows are base change maps.

nodes.title: Specialization flat pullback
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4L}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4L}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field
$\kappa$. Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $R$.
Let $f : X' \to X$ be a morphism which is locally of finite type, flat,
and of relative dimension $e$. Then the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}Z_{r + e}(X'_K) \underset{sp_{X'/R}}{\longrightarrow} &  & Z_{r + e}(X'_\kappa) \\ Z_r(X_K) \overset{sp_{X/R}}{\longrightarrow}\uparrow &  & Z_r(X_\kappa) \uparrow\end{array}
$$
commutes where $r \geq 0$ and the vertical arrows are given
by flat pullback.

nodes.title: Specialization proper pushforward
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4M}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4M}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and residue field
$\kappa$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes locally of
finite type over $R$. Then the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}Z_r(X_K) \underset{sp_{X/R}}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow &  & Z_r(X_\kappa) \downarrow \\ Z_r(Y_K) \overset{sp_{Y/R}}{\longrightarrow} &  & Z_r(Y_\kappa)\end{array}
$$
commutes where $r \geq 0$ and the vertical arrows are given
by proper pushforward.

nodes.title: Compatibilities
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4P}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4P}}


We have the following compatibilities between the operations above:
(1) base change is functorial,
(2) restriction is a combination of base change and (a special case of)
flat pullback,
(3) flat pullback commutes with base change,
(4) flat pullback is functorial,
(5) proper pushforward commutes with base change,
(6) proper pushforward is functorial, and
(7) proper pushforward commutes with flat pullback.

nodes.title: Family associated module
Family associated closed
Support family
Coequalizer dim r
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4W}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4W}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $g : S' \to S$ be a surjective morphism of
schemes. Set $S'' = S' \times_S S'$ and let $f' : X' \to S'$
and $f'' : X'' \to S''$ be the base changes of $f$.
Let $x \in X$ with $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(x))}(\kappa(x)) = r$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists an $x' \in X'$ mapping to $x$
with $\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f'(x'))}(\kappa(x')) = r$.
\item If $x'_1, x'_2 \in X'$ are both as in (1), then there
exists an $x'' \in X''$ with
$\text{trdeg}_{\kappa(f''(x''))}(\kappa(x'')) = r$ and
$\text{pr}_i(x'') = x'_i$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Descend family
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4X}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4X}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $g : S' \to S$ be a morphism of
schemes and $X' = S' \times_S X$. Assume that for every $s \in S$ there
exists a point $s' \in S'$ with $g(s') = s$ and such that
$\kappa(s')/\kappa(s)$ is a separable extension of fields. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item For families $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$
if $g^*\alpha_1 = g^*\alpha_2$, then $\alpha_1 = \alpha_2$.
\item Given a family $\alpha'$ of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X'/S'$ if
$\text{pr}_1^*\alpha' = \text{pr}_2^*\alpha'$ as families of
$r$-cycles on fibres of $(S' \times_S S') \times_S X / (S' \times_S S')$,
then there is a unique family $\alpha$ of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$
such that $g^*\alpha = \alpha'$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Pullback universally bijective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H4Y}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H4Y}}


Let $g : S' \to S$ be a bijective morphism of schemes
which induces isomorphisms of residue fields.
Let $f : X \to S$ be locally of finite type. Set $X' = S' \times_S X$.
Let $r \geq 0$. Then base change by $g$ determines a bijection
between the group of families of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$ and
the group of families of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X'/S'$.

nodes.title: Relative cycles
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H50}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H50}}


Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of
schemes which is locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer.
A {\it relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$} is a family $\alpha$ of $r$-cycles
on fibres of $X/S$ such that for every morphism $g : S' \to S$
where $S'$ is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring we have
$$
sp_{X'/S'}(\alpha_\eta) = \alpha_0
$$
where $sp_{X'/S'}$ is as in Section \ref{relative-cycles-section-specialization}
and $\alpha_\eta$ (resp.\ $\alpha_0$) is the value of the base change
$g^*\alpha$ of $\alpha$ at the generic (resp.\ closed) point of $S'$.
The group of all relative $r$-cycles on $X/S$ is denoted $z(X/S, r)$.

nodes.title: Relative cycle functoriality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H51}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H51}}


Let $\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$ as in
Definition \ref{relative-cycles-definition-relative-cycles}.
Then any restriction, base change, flat pullback, or proper pushforward
of $\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle.

nodes.title: Relative cycles h descent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H52}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H52}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a family of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$. Let $\{g_i : S_i \to S\}$
be a h covering (More on Flatness, Definition
\ref{flat-definition-h-covering}). Then $\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle
if and only if each base change $g_i^*\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle.

nodes.title: Families specialization fppf descent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H53}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H53}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$ be integers.
Let $\alpha$ be a family of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$.
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}$ be a jointly surjective family
of flat morphisms, locally of finite type, and of relative dimension $e$.
Then $\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle if and only if each flat
pullback $f_i^*\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle.

nodes.title: Check after closed
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H54}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H54}}


Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $i : X \to Y$ be a closed immersion
of schemes locally of finite type over $S$. Let $r \geq 0$.
Let $\alpha$ be a family of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$.
Then $\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$ if and only if
$i_*\alpha$ is a relative $r$-cycle on $Y/S$.

nodes.title: Uniqueness extension
Family associated module specialization
Family associated closed specialization
Get cycles
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H59}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H59}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes with $S$ Noetherian.
Let $r \geq 0$. Let $\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. Then there is
a proper, completely decomposed
(More on Morphisms, Definition \ref{more-morphisms-definition-cd-morphism})
morphism $g : S' \to S$ such that $g^*\alpha$ is in the image of
(\ref{equation-cycle-classes}).

nodes.title: Get cycles dvr
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5A}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5A}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes with $S$
the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring. Let $r \geq 0$.
Then (\ref{equation-cycle-classes}) is surjective.

nodes.title: Relative cycle smooth
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5B}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5B}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $r \geq 0$. Assume $S$
locally Noetherian and $f$ smooth of relative dimension $r$. Let
$\alpha \in z(X/S, r)$. Then the support of $\alpha$ is open and closed in $X$
(see proof for a more precise result).

nodes.title: Relative cycles equal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5C}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5C}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ and
$\alpha, \beta \in z(X/S, r)$. The set $E = \{s \in S : \alpha_s = \beta_s\}$
is closed in $S$.

nodes.title: Descend through limit
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5D}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5D}}


Let $S = \lim_{i \in I} S_i$ be the limit of a directed inverse system of
Noetherian schemes with affine transition morphisms.
Let $0 \in I$ and let $X_0 \to S_0$ be a finite type morphism of schemes.
For $i \geq 0$ set $X_i = S_i \times_{S_0} X_0$ and set
$X = S \times_{S_0} X_0$. If $S$ is Noetherian too, then
$$
z(X/S, r) = \colim_{i \geq 0} z(X_i/S_i, r)
$$
where the transition maps are given by base change of relative
$r$-cycles.

nodes.title: Thickening
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5E}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5E}}


Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $i : X \to X'$ be a thickening
of schemes locally of finite type over $S$. Let $r \geq 0$.
Then $i_* : z(X/S, r) \to z(X'/S, r)$ is a bijection.

nodes.title: Extend to larger
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5F}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5F}}


Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $X$ be a scheme locally
of finite type over $S$. Let $r \geq 0$. Let $U \subset X$ be an open
such that $X \setminus U$ has relative dimension $< r$ over $S$, i.e.,
$\dim(X_s \setminus U_s) < r$ for all $s \in S$. Then
restriction defines a bijection $z(X/S, r) \to z(U/S, r)$.

nodes.title: Seminormalize base
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5G}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5G}}


Let $g : S' \to S$ be a universal homeomorphism of locally Noetherian schemes
which induces isomorphisms of residue fields. Let $f : X \to S$ be locally of
finite type. Set $X' = S' \times_S X$. Let $r \geq 0$. Then base change by $g$
determines a bijection $z(X/S, r) \to z(X'/S', r)$.

nodes.title: Equidimensional
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5I}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5I}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian
and $f$ is locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. We say a
relative $r$-cycle $\alpha$ on $X/S$ {\it equidimensional} if the support
of $\alpha$ (Remark \ref{relative-cycles-remark-supports-family})
is contained in a closed subset $W \subset X$ whose relative
dimension over $S$ is $\leq r$.
The group of all equidimensional relative $r$-cycles on $X/S$ is
denoted $z_{equi}(X/S, r)$.

nodes.title: Equidimensional functoriality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5K}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5K}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian
and $f$ is locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let
$\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. If $\alpha$ is equidimensional,
then any restriction, base change, or flat pullback of $\alpha$ is
equidimensional.

nodes.title: Check equidimensional
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5L}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5L}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. Then to check that $\alpha$ is equidimensional
we may work Zariski locally on $X$ and $S$.

nodes.title: Equidimensional fppf descent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5M}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5M}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. Let $\{g_i : S_i \to S\}$
be an fppf covering. Then $\alpha$ is equidimensional
if and only if each base change $g_i^*\alpha$ is equidimensional.

nodes.title: Equidimensional descent pullbacks
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5N}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5N}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$ be integers.
Let $\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$.
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}$ be a jointly surjective family
of flat morphisms, locally of finite type, and of relative dimension $e$.
Then $\alpha$ is equidimensional if and only if each flat
pullback $f_i^*\alpha$ is equidimensional.

nodes.title: Weightings pre
nodes.statement:
In the situation above, if $g : S' \to S$ is a morphism of locally
Noetherian schemes, then $w_{g^*\alpha} = w_\alpha \circ g'$ where
$g' : X' \to X$ is the projection $X' = S' \times_S X \to X$.

nodes.title: Weightings
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5P}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5P}}


Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $f : X \to S$ be a locally
quasi-finite morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $\alpha \in z(X/S, 0)$ the map $w_\alpha : X \to \mathbf{Z}$
constructed above is a weighting.
\item If $X$ is quasi-compact, then given a weighting
$w : X \to \mathbf{Z}$ there exists an integer $n > 0$ such
that $nw = w_\alpha$ for some $\alpha \in z(X/S, 0)$.
\item The integer $n$ in (2) may be chosen to be a power of
the prime $p$ if $S$ is a scheme over $\mathbf{F}_p$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Effective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5R}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5R}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian
and $f$ is locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. We say a
relative $r$-cycle $\alpha$ on $X/S$ {\it effective} if $\alpha_s$ is an
effective cycle
(Chow Homology, Definition \ref{chow-definition-effective-cycle})
for all $s \in S$. The monoid of all effective relative $r$-cycles
on $X/S$ is denoted $z^{eff}(X/S, r)$.

nodes.title: Effective functoriality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5S}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5S}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian
and $f$ is locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let
$\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. If $\alpha$ is effective,
then any restriction, base change, flat pullback, or proper pushforward
of $\alpha$ is effective.

nodes.title: Check effective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5T}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5T}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. Then to check that $\alpha$ is effective
we may work Zariski locally on $X$ and $S$.

nodes.title: Effective descent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5U}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5U}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. Let $g : S' \to S$ be a surjective morphism.
Then $\alpha$ is effective if and only if the base change $g^*\alpha$
is effective.

nodes.title: Effective descent pullbacks
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5V}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5V}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$ be integers.
Let $\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$.
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}$ be a jointly surjective family
of flat morphisms, locally of finite type, and of relative dimension $e$.
Then $\alpha$ is effective if and only if each flat
pullback $f_i^*\alpha$ is effective.

nodes.title: Effective support closed
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5W}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5W}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$ be integers.
Let $\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$.
If $\alpha$ is effective, then $\text{Supp}(\alpha)$ is
closed in $X$.

nodes.title: Effective equidimensional
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H5X}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H5X}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$ be integers.
Let $\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$.
If $\alpha$ is effective, then $\alpha$ is equidimensional.

nodes.title: Proper
Proper functoriality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H62}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H62}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian
and $f$ is locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let
$\alpha$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. If $\alpha$ is proper,
then any base change $\alpha$ is proper.

nodes.title: Proper h descent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H63}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H63}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $S$ locally Noetherian
and $f$ locally of finite type. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer. Let $\alpha$
be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/S$. Let $\{g_i : S_i \to S\}$
be a h covering. Then $\alpha$ is proper
if and only if each base change $g_i^*\alpha$ is proper.

nodes.title: Action bilinear
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H66}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H66}}


The construction above is bilinear, i.e., we have
$(\alpha_1 + \alpha_2) \cap \beta = \alpha_1 \cap \beta +
\alpha_2 \cap \beta$ and $\alpha \cap (\beta_1 + \beta_2) =
\alpha \cap \beta_1 + \alpha \cap \beta_2$.

nodes.title: Action opens
Action base change
Action coherent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H69}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H69}}


Let $(S, \delta)$ and $f : X \to Y$ be as above.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
with $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}_y)) \leq r$ for all $y \in Y$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module
with $\dim_\delta(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{G})) \leq e$.
Set $\alpha = [\mathcal{F}/X/Y]_r$
(Example \ref{relative-cycles-example-family-associated-module}) and
$\beta = [\mathcal{G}]_e$ (Chow Homology, Definition
\ref{chow-definition-cycle-associated-to-coherent-sheaf}).
If $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $Y$, then $\alpha \cap \beta =
[\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} f^*\mathcal{G}]_{r + e}$.

nodes.title: Action closed
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6A}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6A}}


Let $(S, \delta)$ and $f : X \to Y$ be as above. Let $Z \subset X$
be a closed subscheme of relative dimension $\leq r$ over $Y$.
Set $\alpha = [Z/X/Y]_r$ (Example \ref{relative-cycles-example-family-associated-closed}).
Let $W \subset Y$ be a closed subscheme of $\delta$-dimension $\leq e$.
Set $\beta = [W]_e$ (Chow Homology, Definition
\ref{chow-definition-cycle-associated-to-closed-subscheme}).
If $Z$ is flat over $Y$, then $\alpha \cap \beta = [Z \times_Y W]_{r + e}$.

nodes.title: Flat pullback as action
nodes.statement:
Let $(S, \delta)$ and $f : X \to Y$ be as above. Assume
$f$ is flat of relative dimension $e$. For $\beta \in Z_r(Y)$
we have $f^*\beta = [X/X/Y]_e \cap \beta$ in $Z_{e + r}(X)$.

nodes.title: Action push pull
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6B}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6B}}


Let $(S, \delta)$ be as above. Let
$$
\begin{array}{cc}X' \underset{f}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow & X \downarrow \\ Y' \overset{g}{\longrightarrow} & Y\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of schemes locally of finite type over $S$
with $g$ proper. Let $r, e \geq 0$. Let $\alpha$ be a family of
$r$-cycles on the fibres of $X/Y$. Let $\beta' \in Z_e(Y')$.
Then we have $f_*(g^*\alpha \cap \beta') = \alpha \cap g_*\beta'$.

nodes.title: Closed in X gysin
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6D}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6D}}


Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Section \ref{relative-cycles-section-action}.
Let $f : X' \to X$ be a proper morphism of schemes
locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $(\mathcal{L}, s, i : D \to X)$ be as in
Chow Homology, Definition \ref{chow-definition-gysin-homomorphism}.
Form the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}D' \underset{g}{\downarrow}\underset{i'}{\longrightarrow} & X' \overset{f}{\downarrow} \\ D \overset{i}{\longrightarrow} & X\end{array}
$$
as in Chow Homology, Remark \ref{chow-remark-pullback-pairs}.
If $\mathcal{L}|_D \cong \mathcal{O}_D$, then
$i^*f_*\alpha' = g_*(i')^*\alpha'$ in $Z_k(D)$
for any $\alpha' \in Z_{k + 1}(X')$.

nodes.title: Action gysin
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6E}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6E}}


Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Section \ref{relative-cycles-section-action}.
Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes
locally of finite type over $S$. Let $r \geq 0$ and let
$\alpha \in z(X/Y, r)$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/Y$.
Let $(\mathcal{L}, s, i : D \to Y)$ be as in
Chow Homology, Definition \ref{chow-definition-gysin-homomorphism}.
Form the cartesian diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}E \downarrow\underset{j}{\longrightarrow} & X \downarrow \\ D \overset{i}{\longrightarrow} & Y\end{array}
$$
See Chow Homology, Remark \ref{chow-remark-pullback-pairs}.
If $\mathcal{L}|_D \cong \mathcal{O}_D$, then for $e \in \mathbf{Z}$
the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}Z_e(D) \underset{i^*\alpha \cap -}{\longrightarrow} &  & Z_{e + r}(E) \\ Z_{e + 1}(Y) \overset{i^*}{\uparrow}\overset{\alpha \cap -}{\longrightarrow} &  & Z_{r + e + 1}(X) \underset{j^*}{\uparrow}\end{array}
$$
commutes where the vertical arrows $i^*$ and $j^*$ are the
Gysin maps on cycles as in
Chow Homology, Remark \ref{chow-remark-gysin-on-cycles}.

nodes.title: Get bivariant class
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6F}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6F}}


Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Section \ref{relative-cycles-section-action}. Let $X \to Y$
be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $S$. Let $r \geq 0$
and let $\alpha \in z(X/Y, r)$ be a relative $r$-cycle on $X/Y$.
The rule that to every morphism $g : Y' \to Y$ locally of finite type
and every $e \in \mathbf{Z}$ associates the operation
$$
g^*\alpha \cap - : Z_e(Y') \to Z_{r + e}(X')
$$
where $X' = Y' \times_Y X$ factors through rational equivalence to
define a bivariant class $c(\alpha) \in A^{-r}(X \to Y)$.

nodes.title: Construction bilinear
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6I}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6I}}


The construction above is bilinear, i.e., we have
$(\alpha_1 + \alpha_2) \circ \beta \alpha_1 \circ \beta +
\alpha_1 \circ \beta$ and $\alpha \circ (\beta_1 + \beta_2) =
\alpha \circ \beta_1 + \alpha \circ \beta_2$.

nodes.title: Construction opens
Construction base change
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6K}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6K}}


The formation of $\alpha \circ \beta$ is compatible with base change.

nodes.title: Construction coherent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6L}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6L}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ and $Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes, both locally of
finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module of finite type, with
$\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}_y)) \leq r$ for all $y \in Y$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$  be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module of finite
type, with $\dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{G}_s)) \leq e$ for all $s \in S$.
If $\alpha = [\mathcal{F}/X/Y]_r$ and $\beta = [\mathcal{G}/Y/S]_e$
(Example \ref{relative-cycles-example-family-associated-module}) and $\mathcal{F}$
is flat over $Y$, then $\alpha \circ \beta =
[\mathcal{F} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} f^*\mathcal{G}/X/S]_{r + e}$.

nodes.title: Construction closed
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6M}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6M}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ and $Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes, both locally of
finite type. Let $r, e \geq 0$. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed
subscheme of relative dimension $\leq r$ over $Y$.
Let $W \subset Y$ be a closed subscheme of relative dimension $\leq e$
over $S$. If $\alpha = [Z/X/Y]_r$ and $\beta = [W/Y/S]_e$
(Example \ref{relative-cycles-example-family-associated-closed}) and $Z$ is flat over $Y$,
then $\alpha \circ \beta = [Z \times_Y W/X/S]_{r + e}$.

nodes.title: Flat pullback as composition
nodes.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $Y \to S$ be morphisms of schemes, both locally of
finite type. Assume $f$ is flat of relative dimension $e$. Let $\beta$ be
a family of $r$-cycles on the fibres of $Y/S$. Then
$f^*\beta = [X/X/Y]_e \circ \beta$
as families of $(e + r)$-cycles on $X/S$.

nodes.title: Construction push pull
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6N}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6N}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
$$
\begin{array}{cc}X' \underset{f}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow & X \downarrow \\ Y' \overset{g}{\longrightarrow} & Y\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of schemes locally of finite type over $S$
with $g$ proper. Let $r, e \geq 0$. Let $\alpha$ be a family of
$r$-cycles on the fibres of $X/Y$. Let $\beta'$ be a family of
$e$-cycles on the fibres of $Y'/S$. Then we have
$f_*(g^*(\alpha) \circ \beta') = \alpha \circ g_*\beta'$.

nodes.title: Construction composition
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6P}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6P}}


Let $(S, \delta)$ be as in Chow Homology, Situation \ref{chow-situation-setup}.
Let $X \to Y \to Z$ be morphisms of schemes locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $r, s, e \geq 0$. Then
$$
(\alpha \circ \beta) \cap \gamma = \alpha \cap (\beta \cap \gamma)
\quad\text{in}\quad Z_{r + s + e}(X)
$$
where $\alpha$ is a family of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/Y$,
$\beta$ is a family of $s$-cycles on fibres of $Y/Z$, and $\gamma \in Z_e(Z)$.

nodes.title: Well defined
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6R}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6R}}


If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are relative cycles, then so is $\alpha \circ \beta$.

nodes.title: Composition fundamental cycles
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6S}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6S}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to S$ be a morphisms of schemes.
Assume $S$ locally Noetherian, $g$ locally of finite type and
flat of relative dimension $e \ge 0$, and $f$ locally of finite type
and flat of relative dimension $r \geq 0$. Then
$[X/X/Y]_r \circ [Y/Y/S]_e = [X/X/S]_{r + e}$ in $z(X/S, r + e)$.

nodes.title: Relative r cycle general
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H6W}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H6W}}


Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of finite presentation.
Let $r \geq 0$ and let $\alpha$ be a family of $r$-cycles on fibres of $X/S$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a cartesian diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}X \longrightarrow\downarrow & X_0 \downarrow \\ S \longrightarrow & S_0\end{array}
$$
where $X_0 \to S_0$ is a finite type morphism of Noetherian schemes
and $\alpha_0 \in z(X_0/S_0, r)$ such that $\alpha$ is the base change
of $\alpha_0$ by $S \to S_0$
\item there exists a completely decomposed proper morphism $g : S' \to S$
of finite presentation such that $g^*\alpha$ is in the image of
(\ref{equation-cycle-classes-general}).
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Trace well defined
Trace higher
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AX5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AX5}}


Let $\mathbf{F}_p \subset \Lambda \subset R \subset S$ be ring extensions
and assume that $S$ is isomorphic to $R[x]/(x^p - a)$ for some $a \in R$.
Then there are canonical $R$-linear maps
$$
\text{Tr} :
\Omega^{t + 1}_{S/\Lambda}
\longrightarrow
\Omega_{R/\Lambda}^{t + 1}
$$
for $t \geq 0$ such that
$$
\eta_1 \wedge \ldots \wedge \eta_t \wedge x^i\text{d}x
\longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
0 & \text{if} & 0 \leq i \leq p - 2, \\
\eta_1 \wedge \ldots \wedge \eta_t \wedge \text{d}a & \text{if} & i = p - 1
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
for $\eta_i \in \Omega_{R/\Lambda}$ and such that $\text{Tr}$ annihilates the
image of
$S \otimes_R \Omega_{R/\Lambda}^{t + 1} \to \Omega_{S/\Lambda}^{t + 1}$.

nodes.title: Trace extends
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AX6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AX6}}



Let $S$ be a scheme over $\mathbf{F}_p$. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a finite morphism
of Noetherian normal integral schemes over $S$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the extension of function fields is purely inseparable of degree $p$, and
\item $\Omega_{X/S}$ is a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module (for example
if $X$ is of finite type over $S$).
\end{enumerate}
For $i \geq 1$ there is a canonical map
$$
\text{Tr} : f_*\Omega^i_{Y/S} \longrightarrow (\Omega_{X/S}^i)^{**}
$$
whose stalk in the generic point of $X$ recovers the trace map of
Lemma \ref{resolve-lemma-trace-higher}.

nodes.title: Blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AGQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AGQ}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $2$.
Let $f : X \to S = \Spec(A)$ be the blowing up of $A$ in $\mathfrak m$
wotj exceptional divisor $E$. There is a closed immersion
$$
r : X \longrightarrow \mathbf{P}^1_S
$$
over $S$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $r|_E : E \to \mathbf{P}^1_\kappa$ is an isomorphism,
\item $\mathcal{O}_X(E) = \mathcal{O}_X(-1) =
r^*\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^1}(-1)$, and
\item $\mathcal{C}_{E/X} = (r|_E)^*\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^1}(1)$ and
$\mathcal{N}_{E/X} = (r|_E)^*\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}^1}(-1)$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Blowup regular
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AGR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AGR}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $2$.
Let $f : X \to S = \Spec(A)$ be the blowing up of $A$ in $\mathfrak m$.
Then $X$ is an irreducible regular scheme.

nodes.title: Blowup pic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5G}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5G}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $2$.
Let $f : X \to S = \Spec(A)$ be the blowing up of $A$ in $\mathfrak m$.
Then $\Pic(X) = \mathbf{Z}$ generated by $\mathcal{O}_X(E)$.

nodes.title: Cohomology of blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AGS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AGS}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $2$.
Let $f : X \to S = \Spec(A)$ be the blowing up of $A$ in $\mathfrak m$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $p \not \in \{0, 1\}$,
\item $H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n)) = 0$ for $n \geq -1$,
\item $H^1(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ if $\mathcal{F}$ or $\mathcal{F}(1)$
is globally generated,
\item $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n)) = \mathfrak m^{\max(0, n)}$,
\item $\text{length}_A H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n)) = -n(-n - 1)/2$
if $n < 0$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Blowup improve
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AGT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AGT}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $2$.
Let $f : X \to S = \Spec(A)$ be the blowing up of $A$ in $\mathfrak m$.
Let $\mathfrak m^n \subset I \subset \mathfrak m$ be an ideal.
Let $d \geq 0$ be the largest integer such that
$$
I \mathcal{O}_X \subset \mathcal{O}_X(-dE)
$$
where $E$ is the exceptional divisor. Set
$\mathcal{I}' = I\mathcal{O}_X(dE) \subset \mathcal{O}_X$.
Then $d > 0$, the sheaf
$\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}'$ is supported in finitely many
closed points $x_1, \ldots, x_r$ of $X$, and
\begin{align*}
\text{length}_A(A/I)
& >
\text{length}_A \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}') \\
& \geq
\sum\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, r}
\text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, x_i}}
(\mathcal{O}_{X, x_i}/\mathcal{I}'_{x_i})
\end{align*}

nodes.title: Differentials of blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4L}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4L}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $2$.
Let $f : X \to S = \Spec(A)$ be the blowing up of $A$ in $\mathfrak m$.
Then $\Omega_{X/S} = i_*\Omega_{E/\kappa}$, where $i : E \to X$
is the immersion of the exceptional divisor.

nodes.title: Make ideal principal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AHH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AHH}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $T \subset X$ be a finite set of
closed points $x$ such that $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is
regular of dimension $2$ for $x \in T$.
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$ be a quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals such that $\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}$ is supported
on $T$.
Then there exists a sequence
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 = X
$$
where $X_{i + 1} \to X_i$ is the blowing up of $X_i$ at a closed
point lying above a point of $T$ such that
$\mathcal{I}\mathcal{O}_{X_n}$ is an invertible ideal sheaf.

nodes.title: Dominate by blowing up in points
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AHI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AHI}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $T \subset X$ be a finite set of
closed points $x$ such that $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is a regular local
ring of dimension $2$. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a proper morphism of
schemes which is an isomorphism over $U = X \setminus T$.
Then there exists a sequence
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 = X
$$
where $X_{i + 1} \to X_i$ is the blowing up of $X_i$ at a closed
point $x_i$ lying above a point of $T$ and a factorization $X_n \to Y \to X$
of the composition.

nodes.title: Extend rational map blowing up
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5H}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5H}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$ which is
regular and has dimension $2$. Let $Y$ be a proper
scheme over $S$. Given an $S$-rational map $f : U \to Y$ from
$X$ to $Y$ there exists a sequence
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 = X
$$
and an $S$-morphism $f_n : X_n \to Y$ such that $X_{i + 1} \to X_i$
is the blowing up of $X_i$ at a closed point not lying over $U$
and $f_n$ and $f$ agree.

nodes.title: Normalized blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BBS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BBS}}


Let $X$ be a scheme such that every quasi-compact open has finitely
many irreducible components. Let $x \in X$ be a closed point.
The {\it normalized blowup of $X$ at $x$} is the composition
$X'' \to X' \to X$ where $X' \to X$ is the blowup
of $X$ in $x$ and $X'' \to X'$ is the normalization of $X'$.

nodes.title: Nagata normalized blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BFT}}



In Definition \ref{resolve-definition-normalized-blowup} if $X$ is Nagata,
then the normalized blowing up of $X$ at $x$ is
normal, Nagata, and proper over $X$.

nodes.title: Dominate by normalized blowing up
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BBT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BBT}}


Let $X$ be a scheme which is Noetherian, Nagata, and has dimension $2$.
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a proper birational morphism.
Then there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}X_n \longrightarrow\downarrow & X_{n - 1} \longrightarrow & \ldots \longrightarrow & X_1 \longrightarrow & X_0 \downarrow \\ Y \longrightarrow &  &  &  & X\end{array}
$$
where $X_0 \to X$ is the normalization and
where $X_{i + 1} \to X_i$ is the normalized blowing up of $X_i$ at a closed
point.

nodes.title: Extend rational map normalized blowing up
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5I}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5I}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a scheme over $S$ which is
Noetherian, Nagata, and has dimension $2$. Let $Y$ be a proper
scheme over $S$. Given an $S$-rational map $f : U \to Y$ from
$X$ to $Y$ there exists a sequence
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 \to X
$$
and an $S$-morphism $f_n : X_n \to Y$ such that $X_0 \to X$ is the
normalization, $X_{i + 1} \to X_i$ is the normalized blowing up of
$X_i$ at a closed point, and $f_n$ and $f$ agree.

nodes.title: Equivalence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BFV}}


The functor $F$ (\ref{equation-equivalence}) is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Equivalence properties
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BFW}}


Let $S, s_i, S_i$ be as in (\ref{equation-equivalence}).
If $f : X \to S$ corresponds to $g_i : Y_i \to S_i$ under $F$,
then $f$ is separated, proper, finite, if and only if $g_i$ is so
for $i = 1, \ldots, n$.

nodes.title: Equivalence fibre
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BFX}}


Let $S, s_i, S_i$ be as in (\ref{equation-equivalence}).
If $f : X \to S$ corresponds to $g_i : Y_i \to S_i$ under $F$,
then $X_{s_i} \cong (Y_i)_{s_i}$ as schemes over $\kappa(s_i)$.

nodes.title: Equivalence sequence blowups
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BFY}}


Let $S, s_i, S_i$ be as in (\ref{equation-equivalence})
and assume $f : X \to S$ corresponds to $g_i : Y_i \to S_i$ under $F$.
Then there exists a factorization
$$
X = Z_m \to Z_{m - 1} \to \ldots \to Z_1 \to Z_0 = S
$$
of $f$ where $Z_{j + 1} \to Z_j$ is the blowing up of $Z_j$ at a closed
point $z_j$ lying over $\{s_1, \ldots, s_n\}$ if and only if for each
$i$ there exists a factorization
$$
Y_i = Z_{i, m_i} \to Z_{i, m_i - 1} \to \ldots \to Z_{i, 1} \to Z_{i, 0} = S_i
$$
of $g_i$ where $Z_{i, j + 1} \to Z_{i, j}$ is the blowing up of $Z_{i, j}$
at a closed point $z_{i, j}$ lying over $s_i$.

nodes.title: Equivalence sequence normalized blowups
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BFZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BFZ}}


Let $S, s_i, S_i$ be as in (\ref{equation-equivalence})
and assume $f : X \to S$ corresponds to $g_i : Y_i \to S_i$ under $F$.
Assume every quasi-compact open of $S$ has finitely many irreducible
components.  Then there exists a factorization
$$
X = Z_m \to Z_{m - 1} \to \ldots \to Z_1 \to Z_0 = S
$$
of $f$ where $Z_{j + 1} \to Z_j$ is the normalized blowing up of $Z_j$
at a closed point $z_j$ lying over $\{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$ if and only if
for each $i$ there exists a factorization
$$
Y_i = Z_{i, m_i} \to Z_{i, m_i - 1} \to \ldots \to Z_{i, 1} \to Z_{i, 0} = S_i
$$
of $g_i$ where $Z_{i, j + 1} \to Z_{i, j}$ is the normalized blowing up of
$Z_{i, j}$ at a closed point $z_{i, j}$ lying over $s_i$.

nodes.title: Situation: Vanishing
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AX8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AX8}}


Here $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local Noetherian normal domain of
dimension $2$. Let $s$ be the closed point of $S = \Spec(A)$ and
$U = S \setminus \{s\}$. Let $f : X \to S$ be a modification.
We denote $C_1, \ldots, C_r$ the irreducible
components of the special fibre $X_s$ of $f$.

nodes.title: Dominate by scheme modification
Nice meromorphic function
Nontrivial normal bundle
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AXA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AXA}}



In Situation \ref{resolve-situation-vanishing} assume $X$ is normal.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a nonempty effective Cartier divisor such that
$Z \subset X_s$ set theoretically.
Then the conormal sheaf of $Z$ is not trivial.
More precisely, there exists an $i$ such that $C_i \subset Z$
and $\deg(\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}|_{C_i}) > 0$.

nodes.title: H1 injective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AXB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AXB}}



In Situation \ref{resolve-situation-vanishing} assume $X$ is normal
and $A$ Nagata. The map
$$
H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \longrightarrow H^1(f^{-1}(U), \mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is injective.

nodes.title: R1 injective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AXC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AXC}}



In Situation \ref{resolve-situation-vanishing} assume $X$ is normal and $A$ Nagata.
Then
$$
\Hom_{D(A)}(\kappa[-1], Rf_*\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is zero. This uses $D(A) = D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)$ to think of
$Rf_*\mathcal{O}_X$ as an object of $D(A)$.

nodes.title: Grauert-Riemenschneider
Exact sequence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AXF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AXF}}



Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian normal local domain
of dimension $2$. Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}X' \underset{f'}{\searrow}\underset{g}{\longrightarrow} &  & X \overset{f}{\swarrow} \\  & \Spec(A) & \end{array}
$$
where $f$ and $f'$ are modifications as in Situation \ref{resolve-situation-vanishing}
and $X$ normal. Then we have a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to H^1(X', \mathcal{O}_{X'}) \to
H^0(X, R^1g_*\mathcal{O}_{X'}) \to 0
$$
Also $\dim(\text{Supp}(R^1g_*\mathcal{O}_{X'})) = 0$
and $R^1g_*\mathcal{O}_{X'}$ is generated by global sections.

nodes.title: Bound a torsion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AXJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AXJ}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local normal Nagata domain
of dimension $2$. Let $a \in A$ be nonzero. There exists an integer $N$ such
that for every modification $f : X \to \Spec(A)$ with $X$ normal the
$A$-module
$$
M_{X, a} = \Coker(A \longrightarrow H^0(Z, \mathcal{O}_Z))
$$
where $Z \subset X$ is cut out by $a$ has length bounded by $N$.

nodes.title: Reduce to rational
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4N}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4N}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local normal Nagata domain
of dimension $2$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We say $A$ {\it defines a rational singularity} if for every
normal modification $X \to \Spec(A)$ we have $H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = 0$.
\item We say that {\it reduction to rational singularities
is possible for $A$} if the length of the $A$-modules
$$
H^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X)
$$
is bounded for all modifications $X \to \Spec(A)$ with $X$ normal.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Rational propagates
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BG0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BG0}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local normal Nagata domain of
dimension $2$ which defines a rational singularity. Let $A \subset B$
be a local extension of domains with the same fraction field
which is essentially of finite type such
that $\dim(B) = 2$ and $B$ normal. Then $B$ defines a rational singularity.

nodes.title: Reduce to rational
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4P}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4P}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local normal Nagata domain
of dimension $2$. If reduction to rational singularities is possible
for $A$, then there exists a finite sequence of normalized blowups
$$
X = X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 = \Spec(A)
$$
in closed points such that for any closed point $x \in X$
the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ defines a rational singularity.
In particular $X \to \Spec(A)$ is a modification and $X$
is a normal scheme projective over $A$.

nodes.title: Go up separable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AXL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AXL}}


Let $A \to B$ be a finite injective local ring map of local normal
Nagata domains of dimension $2$. Assume that the induced extension of
fraction fields is separable. If reduction to rational singularities
is possible for $A$ then it is possible for $B$.

nodes.title: Regular rational
Bound dualizing implies bound
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4S}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4S}}


Let $A$ be a local normal Nagata domain of dimension $2$ which has a
dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$. If there exists a nonzero $d \in A$
such that for all normal modifications $X \to \Spec(A)$ the cokernel of the
trace map
$$
\Gamma(X, \omega_X) \to \omega_A
$$
is annihilated by $d$, then reduction to rational singularities
is possible for $A$.

nodes.title: Compare differentials dualizing
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4T}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4T}}


Let $p$ be a prime number.
Let $A$ be a regular local ring of dimension $2$ and characteristic $p$.
Let $A_0 \subset A$ be a subring such that $\Omega_{A/A_0}$ is free
of rank $r < \infty$. Set $\omega_A = \Omega^r_{A/A_0}$. If $X \to \Spec(A)$
is the result of a sequence of blowups in closed points, then
there exists a map
$$
\varphi_X : (\Omega^r_{X/\Spec(A_0)})^{**} \longrightarrow \omega_X
$$
extending the given identification in the generic point.

nodes.title: Go up degree p
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4U}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4U}}


Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $A$ be a complete regular local ring of
dimension $2$ and characteristic $p$. Let $L/K$ be a degree $p$ inseparable
extension of the fraction field $K$ of $A$. Let $B \subset L$ be the integral
closure of $A$. Then reduction to rational singularities is possible for $B$.

nodes.title: Situation: Rational
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4W}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4W}}


Here $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local normal Nagata domain of
dimension $2$ which defines a rational singularity. Let $s$ be the closed
point of $S = \Spec(A)$ and $U = S \setminus \{s\}$. Let $f : X \to S$
be a modification with $X$ normal.
We denote $C_1, \ldots, C_r$ the irreducible
components of the special fibre $X_s$ of $f$.

nodes.title: Globally generated
Sections powers I rational
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B4Y}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B4Y}}



In Situation \ref{resolve-situation-rational} assume
$E = X_s$ is an effective Cartier divisor.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be the ideal sheaf of $E$. Then
$H^0(X, \mathcal{I}^n) = \mathfrak m^n$ and
$H^1(X, \mathcal{I}^n) = 0$.

nodes.title: Blow up normal rational
Cohomology blow up rational
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B63}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B63}}



In Situation \ref{resolve-situation-rational}.
Let $X$ be the blowup of $\Spec(A)$ in $\mathfrak m$. Let $E \subset X$
be the exceptional divisor. With $\mathcal{O}_X(1) = \mathcal{I}$ as
usual and $\mathcal{O}_E(1) = \mathcal{O}_X(1)|_E$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is a proper Cohen-Macaulay curve over $\kappa$.
\item $\mathcal{O}_E(1)$ is very ample
\item $\deg(\mathcal{O}_E(1)) \geq 1$ and equality holds only if
$A$ is a regular local ring,
\item $H^1(E, \mathcal{O}_E(n)) = 0$ for $n \geq 0$, and
\item $H^0(E, \mathcal{O}_E(n)) = \mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n + 1}$
for $n \geq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Dualizing rational
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BBU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BBU}}



In Situation \ref{resolve-situation-rational} assume $A$ has a
dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$. With $\omega_X$ the dualizing
module of $X$, the trace map $H^0(X, \omega_X) \to \omega_A$ is an
isomorphism and consequently there is a canonical map
$f^*\omega_A \to \omega_X$.

nodes.title: Dualizing blow up rational
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B64}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B64}}



In Situation \ref{resolve-situation-rational} assume $A$ has a
dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$ and is not regular.
Let $X$ be the blowup of $\Spec(A)$ in $\mathfrak m$ with
exceptional divisor $E \subset X$. Let $\omega_X$
be the dualizing module of $X$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_E = \omega_X|_E \otimes \mathcal{O}_E(-1)$,
\item $H^1(X, \omega_X(n)) = 0$ for $n \geq 0$,
\item the map $f^*\omega_A \to \omega_X$ of
Lemma \ref{resolve-lemma-dualizing-rational} is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Rational to gorenstein
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BBV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BBV}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local normal Nagata domain of
dimension $2$ which defines a rational singularity. Assume $A$ has
a dualizing complex. Then there exists a finite sequence of blowups in
singular closed points
$$
X = X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 = \Spec(A)
$$
such that $X_i$ is normal for each $i$ and such that
the dualizing sheaf $\omega_X$ of $X$ is an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

nodes.title: Sequence blowups
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BG2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BG2}}


Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let
$$
(X, p) = (X_0, p_0) \leftarrow (X_1, p_1) \leftarrow (X_2, p_2) \leftarrow
(X_3, p_3) \leftarrow \ldots
$$
be a sequence of blowups such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $p_i$ is closed, maps to $p_{i - 1}$, and
$\kappa(p_i) = \kappa(p_{i - 1})$,
\item there exists an $x_1 \in \mathfrak m_p$ whose image
in $\mathfrak m_{p_i}$, $i > 0$ defines the exceptional divisor
$E_i \subset X_i$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the sequence is obtained from a nonsingular arc $a : T \to X$
as above.

nodes.title: Sequence blowups along arc becomes nonsingular
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BG3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BG3}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local domain of
dimension $2$. Let $A \to R$ be a surjection onto a
complete discrete valuation ring.
This defines a nonsingular arc $a : T = \Spec(R) \to \Spec(A)$. Let
$$
\Spec(A) = X_0 \leftarrow X_1 \leftarrow X_2 \leftarrow X_3 \leftarrow \ldots
$$
be the sequence of blowing ups constructed from $a$.
If $A_\mathfrak p$ is a regular local ring where
$\mathfrak p = \Ker(A \to R)$, then
for some $i$ the scheme $X_i$ is regular at $x_i$.

nodes.title: Iso completions
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BG5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BG5}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local ring with finitely generated
maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Let $X$ be a scheme over $A$.
Let $Y = X \times_{\Spec(A)} \Spec(A^\wedge)$ where
$A^\wedge$ is the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $A$.
For a point $q \in Y$ with image $p \in X$ lying
over the closed point of $\Spec(A)$ the
local ring map $\mathcal{O}_{X, p} \to \mathcal{O}_{Y, q}$
induces an isomorphism on completions.

nodes.title: Port regularity to completion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BG6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BG6}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $X \to \Spec(A)$ be a morphism which is locally of finite type.
Set $Y = X \times_{\Spec(A)} \Spec(A^\wedge)$. Let $y \in Y$ with
image $x \in X$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is regular, then $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is regular,
\item if $y$ is in the closed fibre, then $\mathcal{O}_{Y, y}$ is regular
$\Leftrightarrow \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$ is regular, and
\item If $X$ is proper over $A$, then $X$ is regular
if and only if $Y$ is regular.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Descend admissible blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AFK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AFK}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring with completion $A^\wedge$.
Let $U \subset \Spec(A)$ and $U^\wedge \subset \Spec(A^\wedge)$ be the
punctured spectra. If $Y \to \Spec(A^\wedge)$ is a $U^\wedge$-admissible
blowup, then there exists a $U$-admissible blowup $X \to \Spec(A)$
such that $Y = X \times_{\Spec(A)} \Spec(A^\wedge)$.

nodes.title: Blowup still good
Formally unramified
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BG8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BG8}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a local Noetherian ring. Let
$X$ be a scheme over $A$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A$ is analytically unramified
(Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-analytically-unramified}),
\item $X$ is locally of finite type over $A$, and
\item $X \to \Spec(A)$ is \'etale at the generic points of irreducible
components of $X$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the normalization of $X$ is finite over $X$.

nodes.title: Normalization completion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BG9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BG9}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $X \to \Spec(A)$ be a morphism which is locally of finite type.
Set $Y = X \times_{\Spec(A)} \Spec(A^\wedge)$.
If the complement of the special fibre in $Y$ is normal, then
the normalization $X^\nu \to X$ is finite and the base change
of $X^\nu$ to $\Spec(A^\wedge)$ recovers the normalization of $Y$.

nodes.title: Normalized blowup completion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGA}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local domain whose completion
$A^\wedge$ is normal. Then given any sequence
$$
Y_n \to Y_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to Y_1 \to \Spec(A^\wedge)
$$
of normalized blowups, there exists a sequence of (proper) normalized blowups
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to \Spec(A)
$$
whose base change to $A^\wedge$ recovers the given sequence.

nodes.title: Situation: Rational double point
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGC}}


Here $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Nagata local normal domain of
dimension $2$ which defines a rational singularity, whose completion
is normal, and which is Gorenstein. We assume $A$ is not regular.

nodes.title: Issquare
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGD}}


Let $\kappa$ be a field. Let $I \subset \kappa[x, y]$ be an ideal. Let
$$
a + b x + c y + d x^2 + exy + f y^2 \in I^2
$$
for some $a, b, c, d, e, f \in k$ not all zero. If the colength
of $I$ in $\kappa[x, y]$ is $> 1$, then
$a + b x + c y + d x^2 + exy + f y^2 = j(g + hx + iy)^2$
for some $j, g, h, i \in \kappa$.

nodes.title: Resolve rational double points
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGE}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local normal Nagata
domain of dimension $2$ which defines a rational singularity,
whose completion is normal, and which is Gorenstein.
Then there exists a finite sequence of blowups in
singular closed points
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 = \Spec(A)
$$
such that $X_n$ is regular and such that each intervening
schemes $X_i$ is normal with finitely many singular points
of the same type.

nodes.title: Regular alteration implies
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGG}}


Let $Y$ be a Noetherian integral scheme. Assume there exists an alteration
$f : X \to Y$ with $X$ regular. Then the normalization $Y^\nu \to Y$
is finite and $Y$ has a dense open which is regular.

nodes.title: Algebra helper
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGH}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a local Noetherian ring. Let $B \subset C$
be finite $A$-algebras. Assume that (a) $B$ is a normal ring, and
(b) the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion $C^\wedge$ is a normal ring.
Then $B^\wedge$ is a normal ring.

nodes.title: Regular alteration implies local
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGI}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a local Noetherian domain.
Assume there exists an alteration $f : X \to \Spec(A)$
with $X$ regular. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a nonzero $f \in A$ such that $A_f$ is regular,
\item the integral closure $B$ of $A$ in its fraction field is finite over $A$,
\item the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $B$ is a normal ring, i.e., the
completions of $B$ at its maximal ideals are normal domains, and
\item the generic formal fibre of $A$ is regular.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Resolution
Resolution surface
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGL}}


Let $Y$ be a $2$-dimensional Noetherian integral scheme.
We say $Y$ has a {\it resolution of singularities by normalized blowups}
if there exists a sequence
$$
Y_n \to Y_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to Y_1 \to Y_0 \to Y
$$
where
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y_i$ is proper over $Y$ for $i = 0, \ldots, n$,
\item $Y_0 \to Y$ is the normalization,
\item $Y_i \to Y_{i - 1}$ is a normalized blowup for $i = 1, \ldots, n$, and
\item $Y_n$ is regular.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Existence implies existence by normalized blowing ups
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGM}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Assume $A$ is normal and has dimension $2$.
If $\Spec(A)$ has a resolution of singularities,
then $\Spec(A)$ has a resolution by normalized blowups.

nodes.title: Resolve complete
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGN}}


Let $(A, \mathfrak m, \kappa)$ be a Noetherian complete local ring.
Assume $A$ is a normal domain of dimension $2$. Then $\Spec(A)$ has a
resolution of singularities.

nodes.title: Lipman
Resolve curve
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BI4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BI4}}


Let $Y$ be a one dimensional integral Noetherian scheme.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists an alteration $X \to Y$ with $X$ regular,
\item there exists a resolution of singularities of $Y$,
\item there exists a finite sequence
$Y_n \to Y_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to Y_1 \to Y$ of blowups
in closed points with $Y_n$ regular, and
\item the normalization $Y^\nu \to Y$ is finite.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Blowup curve
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BI5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BI5}}



Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $Y \subset X$ be an integral closed
subscheme of dimension $1$ satisfying the equivalent conditions of
Lemma \ref{resolve-lemma-resolve-curve}. Then there exists a finite sequence
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X
$$
of blowups in closed points such that the strict transform of $Y$
in $X_n$ is a regular curve.

nodes.title: Blowup nonsingular curves meeting at point
Blowup curves
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BI8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BI8}}



Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $Y_i \subset X$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$
be an integral closed subschemes of dimension $1$ each satisfying the
equivalent conditions of Lemma \ref{resolve-lemma-resolve-curve}. Then there
exists a finite sequence
$$
X_n \to X_{n - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X
$$
of blowups in closed points such that the strict transform $Y'_i \subset X_n$
of $Y_i$ in $X_n$ are pairwise disjoint regular curves.

nodes.title: Turn into effective Cartier
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BIB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BIB}}


Let $X$ be a regular scheme of dimension $2$. Let $Z \subset X$
be a proper closed subscheme. There exists a sequence
$$
X_n \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X
$$
of blowing ups in closed points such that the inverse image $Z_n$ of $Z$
in $X_n$ is an effective Cartier divisor.

nodes.title: Embedded resolution
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BIC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BIC}}



Let $X$ be a regular scheme of dimension $2$. Let $Z \subset X$
be a proper closed subscheme such that every irreducible component
$Y \subset Z$ of dimension $1$ satisfies the equivalent conditions of
Lemma \ref{resolve-lemma-resolve-curve}. Then there exists a sequence
$$
X_n \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X
$$
of blowups in closed points such that the inverse image $Z_n$ of $Z$
in $X_n$ is an effective Cartier divisor supported on a strict normal crossings
divisor.

nodes.title: Factor through contraction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5J}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5J}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $E \subset X$ be an
exceptional curve of the first kind. If a contraction $X \to X'$
of $E$ exists, then it has the following universal property:
for every morphism $\varphi : X \to Y$ such that $\varphi(E)$
is a point, there is a unique factorization
$X \to X' \to Y$ of $\varphi$.

nodes.title: Contraction unique
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5K}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5K}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $E \subset X$ be an
exceptional curve of the first kind. If there exists a contraction
of $E$, then it is unique up to unique isomorphism.

nodes.title: Exceptional first kind local
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C2K}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C2K}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $E \subset X$ be an
exceptional curve of the first kind. Let $E_n = nE$ and
denote $\mathcal{O}_n$ its structure sheaf. Then
$$
A = \lim H^0(E_n, \mathcal{O}_n)
$$
is a complete local Noetherian regular local ring of dimension $2$
and $\Ker(A \to H^0(E_n, \mathcal{O}_n))$ is the $n$th power of
its maximal ideal.

nodes.title: Contraction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C2L}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C2L}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $E \subset X$ be an
exceptional curve of the first kind. If there exists a morphism
$f : X \to Y$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is Noetherian,
\item $f$ is proper,
\item $f$ maps $E$ to a point $y$ of $Y$,
\item $f$ is quasi-finite at every point not in $E$,
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a contraction of $E$ and it is the Stein
factorization of $f$.

nodes.title: Pic blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5L}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5L}}


Let $b : X \to X'$ be the contraction of an
exceptional curve of the first kind $E \subset X$.
Then there is a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to \Pic(X') \to \Pic(X) \to \mathbf{Z} \to 0
$$
where the first map is pullback by $b$ and the second map sends
$\mathcal{L}$ to the degree of $\mathcal{L}$ on the exceptional
curve $E$. The sequence is split by the map
$n \mapsto \mathcal{O}_X(-nE)$.

nodes.title: Lift sections and h1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C2J}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C2J}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $E \subset X$ be an
exceptional curve of the first kind. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be
an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $n$ be the integer such that $\mathcal{L}|_E$ has degree $n$
viewed as an invertible module on $\mathbf{P}^1$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) = 0$ and $n \geq 0$, then
$H^1(X, \mathcal{L}(iE)) = 0$ for $0 \leq i \leq n + 1$.
\item If $n \leq 0$, then
$H^1(X, \mathcal{L}) \subset H^1(X, \mathcal{L}(E))$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Contract ample
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C2M}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C2M}}



Let $S = \Spec(R)$ be an affine Noetherian scheme.
Let $X \to S$ be a proper morphism. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an
ample invertible sheaf on $X$. Let $E \subset X$ be an
exceptional curve of the first kind. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a contraction $b : X \to X'$ of $E$,
\item $X'$ is proper over $S$, and
\item the invertible $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module $\mathcal{L}'$
is ample with $\mathcal{L}'$ as in Remark \ref{resolve-remark-pic-blowup}.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Contract when quasi projective
Regular dim 2 quasi projective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5N}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5N}}


Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $f : X \to S$ be a
separated morphism of finite type with $X$ regular of dimension $2$.
Then $X$ is quasi-projective over $S$.

nodes.title: Regular dim 2 projective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5P}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5P}}


Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $f : X \to S$ be a
proper morphism with $X$ regular of dimension $2$.
Then $X$ is projective over $S$.

nodes.title: Proper birational regular surfaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5R}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5R}}
