Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper birational morphism between
integral Noetherian schemes regular of dimension $2$.
Then $f$ is a sequence of blowups in closed points.

nodes.title: Birational regular surfaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5S}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5S}}


Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $X$ and $Y$ be proper
integral schemes over $S$ which are regular of dimension $2$.
Then $X$ and $Y$ are $S$-birational if and only if there
exists a diagram of $S$-morphisms
$$
X = X_0 \leftarrow X_1 \leftarrow \ldots \leftarrow X_n = Y_m
\to \ldots \to Y_1 \to Y_0 = Y
$$
where each morphism is a blowup in a closed point.

nodes.title: Recurring
Recurring real
Recurring symmetric real
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C5X}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C5X}}


Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be a symmetric real $n \times n$ matrix with
$a_{ij} \geq 0$ for $i \not = j$.
Let $m = (m_1, \ldots, m_n)$ be a real vector with $m_i > 0$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Am = 0$,
\item there is no proper nonempty subset $I \subset \{1, \ldots, n\}$
such that $a_{ij} = 0$ for $i \in I$ and $j \not \in I$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $x^t A x \leq 0$ with equality if and only if $x = qm$
for some $q \in \mathbf{R}$.

nodes.title: Orthogonal direct sum
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C6V}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C6V}}


Let $L$ be a finite free $\mathbf{Z}$-module endowed
with an integral symmetric bilinear positive definite
form $\langle\ ,\ \rangle : L \times L \to \mathbf{Z}$.
Let $A \subset L$ be a submodule with $L/A$ torsion free. Set
$B = \{b \in L \mid \langle a, b\rangle = 0,\ \forall a \in A\}$.
Then we have injective maps
$$
A^\#/A \leftarrow L/(A \oplus B) \rightarrow B^\#/B
$$
whose cokernels are quotients of $L^\#/L$. Here
$A^\# = \{a' \in A \otimes \mathbf{Q} \mid
\langle a, a'\rangle \in \mathbf{Z},\ \forall a \in A\}$
and similarly for $B$ and $L$.

nodes.title: Coker
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C6W}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C6W}}



Let $L_0$, $L_1$ be a finite free $\mathbf{Z}$-modules endowed
with integral symmetric bilinear positive definite
forms $\langle\ ,\ \rangle : L_i \times L_i \to \mathbf{Z}$.
Let $\text{d} : L_0 \to L_1$ and $\text{d}^* : L_1 \to L_0$
be adjoint. If $\langle\ ,\ \rangle$ on $L_0$ is unimodular, then
there is an isomorphism
$$
\Phi :
\Coker(\text{d}^*\text{d})_{torsion}
\longrightarrow
\Im(\text{d})^\#/\Im(\text{d})
$$
with notation as in Lemma \ref{models-lemma-orthogonal-direct-sum}.

nodes.title: Recurring symmetric integer
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C6X}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C6X}}


Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be a symmetric $n \times n$ integer matrix with
$a_{ij} \geq 0$ for $i \not = j$. Let $m = (m_1, \ldots, m_n)$ be an
integer vector with $m_i > 0$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Am = 0$,
\item there is no proper nonempty subset $I \subset \{1, \ldots, n\}$
such that $a_{ij} = 0$ for $i \in I$ and $j \not \in I$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $e$ be the number of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j$ and $a_{ij} > 0$.
Then for $\ell$ a prime number coprime with all $a_{ij}$ and $m_i$
we have
$$
\dim_{\mathbf{F}_\ell}(\Coker(A)[\ell]) \leq 1 - n + e
$$

nodes.title: Type
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C6Z}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C6Z}}


A {\it numerical type} $T$ is given by
$$
n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i
$$
where $n \geq 1$ is an integer and $m_i$, $a_{ij}$, $w_i$, $g_i$
are integers for $1 \leq i, j \leq n$ subject to the following conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item $m_i > 0$, $w_i > 0$, $g_i \geq 0$,
\item the matrix $A = (a_{ij})$ is symmetric and $a_{ij} \geq 0$
for $i \not = j$,
\item there is no proper nonempty subset $I \subset \{1, \ldots, n\}$
such that $a_{ij} = 0$ for $i \in I$, $j \not \in I$,
\item for each $i$ we have $\sum_j a_{ij}m_j = 0$, and
\item $w_i | a_{ij}$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Type equivalent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C70}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C70}}


We say two numerical types $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ and
$n', m'_i, a'_{ij}, w'_i, g'_i$ are {\it equivalent types} if
there exists a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$
such that $m_i = m'_{\sigma(i)}$, $a_{ij} = a'_{\sigma(i)\sigma(j)}$,
$w_i = w'_{\sigma(i)}$, and $g_i = g'_{\sigma(i)}$.

nodes.title: Genus
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C71}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C71}}


Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type. Then the expression
$$
g = 1 + \sum m_i(w_i(g_i - 1) - \frac{1}{2} a_{ii})
$$
is an integer.

nodes.title: Genus
Irreducible
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C73}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C73}}



Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type of genus $g$.
If $n = 1$, then $a_{11} = 0$ and $g = 1 + m_1w_1(g_1 - 1)$.
Moreover, we can classify all such numerical types as follows
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $g < 0$, then $g_1 = 0$ and there are finitely many possible
numerical types of genus $g$ with $n = 1$ corresponding to factorizations
$m_1w_1 = 1 - g$.
\item If $g = 0$, then $m_1 = 1$, $w_1 = 1$, $g_1 = 0$
as in Lemma \ref{models-lemma-genus-zero}.
\item If $g = 1$, then we conclude $g_1 = 1$ but $m_1, w_1$ can be arbitrary
positive integers; this is case
(\ref{item-one}) of Lemma \ref{models-lemma-genus-one}.
\item If $g > 1$, then $g_1 > 1$ and there are finitely many possible
numerical types of genus $g$ with $n = 1$ corresponding to
factorizations $m_1w_1(g_1 - 1) = g - 1$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Diagonal negative
Minus one
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C75}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C75}}


Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type of genus $g$.
Assume $n > 1$. If $i$ is such that the contribution
$m_i(w_i(g_i - 1) - \frac{1}{2} a_{ii})$
to the genus $g$ is $< 0$, then $g_i = 0$ and $a_{ii} = -w_i$.

nodes.title: Type minus one
Contract
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C77}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C77}}


Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type $T$.
Assume $n$ is a $(-1)$-index. Then there is a numerical
type $T'$ given by $n', m'_i, a'_{ij}, w'_i, g'_i$ with
\begin{enumerate}
\item $n' = n - 1$,
\item $m'_i = m_i$,
\item $a'_{ij} = a_{ij} - a_{in}a_{jn}/a_{nn}$,
\item $w'_i = w_i/2$ if $a_{in}/w_n$ even and $a_{in}/w_i$ odd
and $w'_i = w_i$ else,
\item $g'_i =
\frac{w_i}{w'_i}(g_i - 1) + 1 + \frac{a_{in}^2 - w_na_{in}}{2w'_iw_n}$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, we have $g = g'$.

nodes.title: Top genus
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C78}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C78}}


Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type.
Let $e$ be the number of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j$ and $a_{ij} > 0$.
Then the expression $g_{top} = 1 - n + e$ is $\geq 0$.

nodes.title: Top genus
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C79}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C79}}



Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type $T$. The
{\it topological genus of $T$} is the nonnegative integer
$g_{top} = 1 - n + e$ from Lemma \ref{models-lemma-top-genus}.

nodes.title: Type minimal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C7A}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C7A}}


We say the numerical type $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ of genus $g$
is {\it minimal} if there does not exist an $i$
with $g_i = 0$ and $a_{ii} = -w_i$, in other words, if there
does not exist a $(-1)$-index.

nodes.title: Non irreducible minimal type genus at least one
Genus nonnegative
Minus two
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C7D}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C7D}}


Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type of genus $g$.
Assume $n > 1$. If $i$ is such that the contribution
$m_i(w_i(g_i - 1) - \frac{1}{2} a_{ii})$
to the genus $g$ is $0$, then $g_i = 0$ and $a_{ii} = -2w_i$.

nodes.title: Type minus two
Picard group
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C7H}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C7H}}


Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type $T$. The
{\it Picard group of $T$} is the cokernel of the matrix
$(a_{ij}/w_i)$, more precisely
$$
\Pic(T) =
\Coker\left(
\mathbf{Z}^{\oplus n} \to \mathbf{Z}^{\oplus n},\quad
e_i
\mapsto
\sum \frac{a_{ij}}{w_j}e_j
\right)
$$
where $e_i$ denotes the $i$th standard basis vector for $\mathbf{Z}^{\oplus n}$.

nodes.title: Picard rank 1
Picard T and A
Contract picard group
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C7J}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C7J}}



Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type $T$.
Assume $n$ is a $(-1)$-index. Let $T'$ be the numerical
type constructed in Lemma \ref{models-lemma-contract}. There exists an
injective map
$$
\Pic(T) \to \Pic(T')
$$
whose cokernel is an elementary abelian $2$-group.

nodes.title: Picard group genus nonpositive
Two by two
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C7M}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C7M}}


Classification of proper subgraphs of the form
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\bullet \longrightarrow & \bullet\end{array}
$$
If $n > 2$, then given a pair $i, j$ of $(-2)$-indices with $a_{ij} > 0$,
then up to ordering we have the $m$'s, $a$'s, $w$'s
\begin{enumerate}
\item

are given by
$$
\left(

m_2
\end{matrix}
\right),
\quad
\left(

w & -2w
\end{matrix}

\quad
\left(
\begin{matrix}
w \\
w
\end{matrix}
\right)
$$
with $w$ arbitrary and $2m_1 \geq m_2$ and $2m_2 \geq m_1$, or

are given by

\left(
\begin{matrix}

m_2

w \\
2w

are given by

\left(

m_2

w \\
3w

\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Three by three
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C7R}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C7R}}


Classification of proper subgraphs of the form
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}\bullet \longrightarrow & \bullet \longrightarrow & \bullet\end{array}
$$
If $n > 3$, then given a triple $i, j, k$ of $(-2)$-indices
with at least two $a_{ij}, a_{ik}, a_{jk}$ nonzero, then up
to ordering we have the $m$'s, $a$'s, $w$'s
\begin{enumerate}
\item

are given by
$$
\left(
\begin{matrix}
m_1 \\
m_2 \\
m_3
\end{matrix}

\quad
\left(
\begin{matrix}
-2w & w & 0 \\
w & -2w & w \\
0 & w & -2w

w \\
w

\right)

with $2m_1 \geq m_2$, $2m_2 \geq m_1 + m_3$, $2m_3 \geq m_2$, or
\item

are given by
$$
\left(
\begin{matrix}
m_1 \\
m_2 \\
m_3
\end{matrix}

\quad
\left(

-2w & w & 0 \\
w & -2w & 2w \\

2w

w

nodes.title: Four by four
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C7V}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C7V}}


Classification of proper subgraphs of the form
$$
\begin{array}{cccc}\bullet \longrightarrow & \bullet \longrightarrow & \bullet \longrightarrow & \bullet\end{array}
$$
If $n > 4$, then given four $(-2)$-indices $i, j, k, l$
with $a_{ij}, a_{jk}, a_{kl}$ nonzero, then up
to ordering we have the $m$'s, $a$'s, $w$'s
\begin{enumerate}
\item

are given by
$$
\left(
\begin{matrix}
m_1 \\
m_2 \\
m_3 \\
m_4
\end{matrix}
\right),
\quad
\left(
\begin{matrix}
-2w & w & 0 & 0 \\
w & -2w & w & 0 \\
0 & w & -2w & w \\
0 & 0 & w & -2w
\end{matrix}
\right),
\quad
\left(
\begin{matrix}
w \\
w \\
w \\
w
\end{matrix}
\right)
$$
with $2m_1 \geq m_2$, $2m_2 \geq m_1 + m_3$, $2m_3 \geq m_2 + m_4$,
and $2m_4 \geq m_3$, or
\item

are given by
$$
\left(
\begin{matrix}
m_1 \\
m_2 \\
m_3 \\
m_4
\end{matrix}
\right),
\quad
\left(

-2w & w & 0 & 0 \\
w & -2w & w & 0 \\

\quad

w \\
w \\
w \\
2w
\end{matrix}
\right)
$$
with $2m_1 \geq m_2$, $2m_2 \geq m_1 + m_3$, $2m_3 \geq m_2 + 2m_4$,
and $2m_4 \geq m_3$, or
\item

are given by
$$
\left(
\begin{matrix}
m_1 \\
m_2 \\
m_3 \\
m_4
\end{matrix}
\right),
\quad
\left(
\begin{matrix}
-4w & 2w & 0 & 0 \\
2w & -4w & 2w & 0 \\
0 & 2w & -4w & 2w \\

\end{matrix}
\right),
\quad
\left(
\begin{matrix}

2w \\
2w \\
w
\end{matrix}

nodes.title: Bound neighbours
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C9U}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C9U}}


Let $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$ be a numerical type of genus $g$.
Given $i, j$ with $a_{ij} > 0$ we have
$m_ia_{ij} \leq m_j|a_{jj}|$ and $m_iw_i \leq m_j|a_{jj}|$.

nodes.title: Bound heart
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C9V}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C9V}}


Fix $g \geq 2$. For every minimal numerical type $n, m_i, a_{ij}, w_i, g_i$
of genus $g$ with $n > 1$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item the set $J \subset \{1, \ldots, n\}$ of non-$(-2)$-indices
has at most $2g - 2$ elements,
\item for $j \in J$ we have $g_j < g$,
\item for $j \in J$ we have $m_j|a_{jj}| \leq 6g - 6$, and
\item for $j \in J$ and $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$
we have $m_ia_{ij} \leq 6g - 6$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Bound wm
Bound picard group
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C9X}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C9X}}



Let $g \geq 2$. For every numerical type $T$ of genus $g$
and prime number $\ell > 768g$ we have
$$
\dim_{\mathbf{F}_\ell} \Pic(T)[\ell] \leq g
$$
where $\Pic(T)$ is as in Definition \ref{models-definition-picard-group}.
If $T$ is minimal, then we even have
$$
\dim_{\mathbf{F}_\ell} \Pic(T)[\ell] \leq g_{top} \leq g
$$
where $g_{top}$ as in Definition \ref{models-definition-top-genus}.

nodes.title: Closure is model
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C2S}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C2S}}


Let $V_1 \to V_2$ be a closed immersion of algebraic schemes over $K$.
If $X_2$ is a model for $V_2$, then the scheme theoretic image
of $V_1 \to X_2$ is a model for $V_1$.

nodes.title: Normalization
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C2T}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C2T}}


Let $X$ be a model of a geometrically normal variety $V$ over $K$.
Then the normalization $\nu : X^\nu \to X$ is finite and
the base change of $X^\nu$ to the completion $R^\wedge$
is the normalization of the base change of $X$. Moreover, for
each $x \in X^\nu$ the completion of $\mathcal{O}_{X^\nu, x}$
is normal.

nodes.title: Regular
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C2U}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C2U}}


Let $X$ be a model of a smooth curve $C$ over $K$. Then
there exists a resolution of singularities of $X$
and any resolution is a model of $C$.

nodes.title: Minimal model
A regular proper model of a curve is obtained by successive blowups from a minimal model
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CD9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CD9}}



Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with
$H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$. If $X$ is a regular proper
model for $C$, then there exists a sequence of morphisms
$$
X = X_m \to X_{m - 1} \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0
$$
of proper regular models of $C$, such that each morphism is a
contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind, and such
that $X_0$ is a minimal model.

\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C61}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C61}}



Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$,
residue field $k$, and uniformizer $\pi$.
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with $H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$.
Let $X$ be a regular proper model of $C$.
Let $C_1, \ldots, C_n$ be the irreducible components of the special
fibre $X_k$. Write $X_k = \sum m_i C_i$ as in
Lemma \ref{models-lemma-divisor-special-fiber}.

nodes.title: Regular model connected
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C62}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C62}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} the special fibre $X_k$ is connected.

nodes.title: Regular model pic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C63}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C63}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} there is an exact sequence
$$
0 \to \mathbf{Z} \to \mathbf{Z}^{\oplus n} \to
\Pic(X) \to \Pic(C) \to 0
$$
where the first map sends $1$ to $(m_1, \ldots, m_n)$ and the second
maps sends the $i$th basis vector to $\mathcal{O}_X(C_i)$.

nodes.title: Intersection pairing
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C64}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C64}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} given $\mathcal{L}$ an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module and
$a = (a_1, \ldots, a_n) \in \mathbf{Z}^{\oplus n}$ we define
$$
\langle a, \mathcal{L} \rangle = \sum a_i\deg(\mathcal{L}|_{C_i})
$$
Then $\langle , \rangle$ is bilinear and for
$b = (b_1, \ldots, b_n) \in \mathbf{Z}^{\oplus n}$ we have
$$
\left\langle a, \mathcal{O}_X(\sum b_i C_i) \right\rangle =
\left\langle b, \mathcal{O}_X(\sum a_i C_i) \right\rangle
$$

nodes.title: Properties form
Multiple fibre normal bundle
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C67}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C67}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} set $d = \gcd(m_1, \ldots, m_n)$
and let $D = \sum (m_i/d)C_i$ as an effective Cartier divisor.
Then $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ has order dividing $d$ in $\Pic(X)$
and $\mathcal{C}_{D/X}$ an invertible $\mathcal{O}_D$-module
of order dividing $d$ in $\Pic(D)$.

nodes.title: Regular model field
Regular model genus
Exceptional curves dont meet
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C6A}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C6A}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} given a pair of indices $i, j$
such that $C_i$ and $C_j$ are exceptional curves of the first kind
and $C_i \cap C_j \not = \emptyset$, then
$n = 2$, $m_1 = m_2 = 1$, $C_1 \cong \mathbf{P}^1_k$,
$C_2 \cong \mathbf{P}^1_k$, $C_1$ and $C_2$ meet in a $k$-rational point,
and $C$ has genus $0$.

nodes.title: Minimal model unique
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C6B}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C6B}}


Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with
$H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$ and genus $> 0$.
There is a unique minimal model for $C$.

nodes.title: Minimal model mapping property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C9Z}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C9Z}}



Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with $H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$
and genus $> 0$. Let $X$ be the minimal model for $C$
(Lemma \ref{models-lemma-minimal-model-unique}).
Let $Y$ be a regular proper model for $C$. Then there is a unique
morphism of models $Y \to X$ which is a sequence of contractions of
exceptional curves of the first kind.

nodes.title: Add component
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CA2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CA2}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} suppose we have an
effective Cartier divisors $D, D' \subset X$ such that
$D' = D + C_i$ for some $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$ and $D' \subset X_k$.
Then
$$
\chi(X_k, \mathcal{O}_{D'}) - \chi(X_k, \mathcal{O}_D) =
\chi(X_k, \mathcal{O}_X(-D)|_{C_i}) =
-(D \cdot C_i) + \chi(C_i, \mathcal{O}_{C_i})
$$

nodes.title: Genus formula
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CA3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CA3}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} we have
$$
g_C = 1 + \sum\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n}
m_i\left([\kappa_i : k] (g_i - 1) - \frac{1}{2}(C_i \cdot C_i)\right)
$$
where $\kappa_i = H^0(C_i, \mathcal{O}_{C_i})$,
$g_i$ is the genus of $C_i$, and $g_C$ is the genus of $C$.

nodes.title: Numerical type of model
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CA4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CA4}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} with
$\kappa_i = H^0(C_i, \mathcal{O}_{C_i})$ and $g_i$ the genus of $C_i$
the data
$$
n, m_i, (C_i \cdot C_j), [\kappa_i : k], g_i
$$
is a numerical type of genus equal to the genus of $C$.

nodes.title: Numerical type model
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CA5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CA5}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} the
{\it numerical type associated to $X$} is the numerical
type described in Lemma \ref{models-lemma-numerical-type-of-model}.

nodes.title: Numerical type minimal model
Numerical type rational point
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CE8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CE8}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} assume $C$ has a $K$-rational point.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X_k$ has a $k$-rational point $x$ which is a smooth point of $X_k$
over $k$,
\item if $x \in C_i$, then $H^0(C_i, \mathcal{O}_{C_i}) = k$ and
$m_i = 1$, and
\item $H^0(X_k, \mathcal{O}_{X_k}) = k$ and $X_k$ has genus equal to
the genus of $C$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Genus reduction smaller
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CE9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CE9}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} assume $X$ is a minimal model,
$\gcd(m_1, \ldots, m_n) = 1$, and $H^0((X_k)_{red}, \mathcal{O}) = k$. Then
the map
$$
H^1(X_k, \mathcal{O}_{X_k}) \to H^1((X_k)_{red}, \mathcal{O}_{(X_k)_{red}})
$$
is surjective and has a nontrivial kernel as soon as $(X_k)_{red} \not = X_k$.

nodes.title: Genus reduction bigger than
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CEA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CEA}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} assume $X_k$ has a $k$-rational
point $x$ which is a smooth point of $X_k \to \Spec(k)$. Then
$$
\dim_k H^1((X_k)_{red}, \mathcal{O}_{(X_k)_{red}}) \geq
g_{top} + g_{geom}(X_k/k)
$$
where $g_{geom}$ is as in
Algebraic Curves, Section \ref{curves-section-genus-geometric-genus}
and $g_{top}$ is the topological genus
(Definition \ref{models-definition-top-genus})
of the numerical type associated to $X_k$
(Definition \ref{models-definition-numerical-type-model}).

nodes.title: Equality genus reduction bigger than
Blowdown regular model
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C6C}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0C6C}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} assume that $C_n$ is
an exceptional curve of the first kind. Let $f : X \to X'$ be the
contraction of $C_n$. Let $C'_i = f(C_i)$. Write $X'_k = \sum m'_i C'_i$.
Then $X'$, $C'_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, n' = n - 1$, and $m'_i = m_i$
is as in Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} and we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item for $i, j < n$ we have
$(C'_i \cdot C'_j) =
(C_i \cdot C_j) - (C_i \cdot C_n) (C_j \cdot C_n) /(C_n \cdot C_n)$,
\item for $i < n$ if $C_i \cap C_n \not = \emptyset$, then there are
maps $\kappa_i \leftarrow \kappa'_i \rightarrow \kappa_n$.
\end{enumerate}
Here $\kappa_i = H^0(C_i, \mathcal{O}_{C_i})$ and
$\kappa'_i = H^0(C'_i, \mathcal{O}_{C'_i})$.

nodes.title: Nonuniqueness
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDA}}


Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with $H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$
and genus $0$. If there is more than one minimal model for $C$, then
the special fibre of every minimal model is isomorphic to $\mathbf{P}^1_k$.

nodes.title: Characterize trivial
Canonical map of pic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CAC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CAC}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model}
let $T$ be the numerical type associated to $X$.
There exists a canonical map
$$
\Pic(C) \to \Pic(T)
$$
whose kernel is exactly those invertible modules on $C$
which are the restriction of invertible modules $\mathcal{L}$
on $X$ with $\deg_{C_i}(\mathcal{L}|_{C_i}) = 0$ for
$i = 1, \ldots, n$.

nodes.title: Sequence torsion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CAD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CAD}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} let $d = \gcd(m_1, \ldots, m_n)$
and let $T$ be the numerical type associated to $X$.
Let $h \geq 1$ be an integer prime to $d$. There exists an exact sequence
$$
0 \to \Pic(X)[h] \to \Pic(C)[h] \to \Pic(T)[h]
$$

nodes.title: Torsion embeds
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CAE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CAE}}



In Situation \ref{models-situation-regular-model} let $h$ be an integer
prime to the characteristic of $k$. Then the map
$$
\Pic(X)[h] \longrightarrow \Pic((X_k)_{red})[h]
$$
is injective.

nodes.title: Etale local at worst nodal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDD}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring. Let $X$ be a scheme which is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$ over $R$.
Let $x \in X$ be a point of the special fibre
of $X$ over $R$. Then there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}X \downarrow & U \longrightarrow\downarrow\longleftarrow & \Spec(A) \swarrow \\ \Spec(R) & \Spec(R') \longleftarrow & \end{array}
$$
where $R \subset R'$ is an \'etale extension of discrete valuation rings,
the morphism $U \to X$ is \'etale, the morphism $U \to \Spec(A)$ is \'etale,
there is a point $x' \in U$ mapping to $x$, and
$$
A = R'[u, v]/(uv)
\quad\text{or}\quad
A = R'[u, v]/(uv - \pi^n)
$$
where $n \geq 0$ and $\pi \in R'$ is a uniformizer.

nodes.title: Blowup at worst nodal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDE}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme which
is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$ with smooth generic fibre over $R$.
Then there exists $m \geq 0$ and a sequence
$$
X_m \to \ldots \to X_1 \to X_0 = X
$$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X_{i + 1} \to X_i$ is the blowing up of a closed point
$x_i$ where $X_i$ is singular,
\item $X_i \to \Spec(R)$ is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$,
\item $X_m$ is regular.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Blowdown at worst nodal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDF}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$
and residue field $k$. Assume $X \to \Spec(R)$ is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$ over $R$.
Let $X \to X'$ be the contraction of an
exceptional curve $E \subset X$ of the first kind.
Then $X'$ is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$ over $R$.

nodes.title: Semistable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDG}}


Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$.
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with $H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a proper model of $C$ which is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$ over $R$,
\item there exists a minimal model of $C$ which is at-worst-nodal
of relative dimension $1$ over $R$, and
\item any minimal model of $C$ is at-worst-nodal
of relative dimension $1$ over $R$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Semistable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDH}}



Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$.
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with $H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$.
We say that $C$ has {\it semistable reduction} if the equivalent
conditions of Lemma \ref{models-lemma-semistable} are satisfied.

nodes.title: Good
Good
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDJ}}



Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$.
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $K$ with $H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$.
We say that $C$ has {\it good reduction} if the equivalent
conditions of Lemma \ref{models-lemma-good} are satisfied.

nodes.title: Semistable reduction
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CDN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CDN}}


\begin{reference}
\cite[Corollary 2.7]{DM}
\end{reference}
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$. Let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $K$ with $H^0(C, \mathcal{O}_C) = K$.
Then there exists an extension of discrete valuation rings
$R \subset R'$ which induces a finite separable extension of
fraction fields $K'/K$ such that $C_{K'}$ has semistable reduction.
More precisely, we have the following
\begin{enumerate}
\item If the genus of $C$ is zero, then there exists a degree $2$
separable extension $K'/K$ such that $C_{K'} \cong \mathbf{P}^1_{K'}$
and hence $C_{K'}$ is isomorphic to the generic fibre of the
smooth projective scheme $\mathbf{P}^1_{R'}$ over the integral closure
$R'$ of $R$ in $K'$.
\item If the genus of $C$ is one, then there exists a finite separable
extension $K'/K$ such that $C_{K'}$ has semistable reduction
over $R'_\mathfrak m$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$
of the integral closure $R'$ of $R$ in $K'$. Moreover, the special
fibre of the (unique) minimal model of $C_{K'}$ over $R'_\mathfrak m$
is either a smooth genus one curve or a cycle of rational curves.
\item If the genus $g$ of $C$ is greater than one, then there exists a
finite separable extension $K'/K$ of degree at most
$B_g$ (\ref{equation-bound}) such that $C_{K'}$ has semistable reduction
over $R'_\mathfrak m$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$
of the integral closure $R'$ of $R$ in $K'$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Baffling
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03SP}}


Let $X$ be a scheme and $g : X \to X$ a morphism. Assume that for all
$\varphi : U \to X$ \'etale, there is an isomorphism
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}U \underset{\varphi}{\searrow}\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} &  & {U
\times_{\varphi, X, g} X} \overset{\text{pr}_2}{\swarrow} \\  & X & \end{array}
$$
functorial in $U$. Then $g$ induces the identity on cohomology (for any sheaf).

nodes.title: The Baffling Theorem
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03SN}}


Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p > 0$. Then the absolute frobenius
induces (by pullback) the trivial map on cohomology, i.e., for all
integers $j\geq 0$,
$$
F_X^* : H^j (X, \underline{\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z}}) \longrightarrow H^j (X,
\underline{\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z}})
$$
is the identity.

nodes.title: Geometric frobenius
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03SQ}}


Let $k$ be a finite field with $q = p^f$ elements. Let $X$ be a scheme
over $k$. The {\it geometric frobenius} of $X$ is the morphism
$\pi_X : X \to X$ over $\Spec(k)$ which equals $F_X^f$.

nodes.title: Sheaf over finite field has frobenius descent
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03SR}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf on $X_\etale$.
Then there are canonical isomorphisms
$\pi_X^{-1} \mathcal{F} \cong \mathcal{F}$ and
$\mathcal{F} \cong {\pi_X}_*\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.title: Two actions agree
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03ST}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03ST}}


In the situation above denote $\alpha : X \to \Spec(k)$ the structure morphism.
Consider the stalk $(R^j\alpha_*\mathcal{F})_{\Spec(\bar k)}$ endowed with its
natural Galois action as in
\'Etale Cohomology, Section \ref{etale-cohomology-section-galois-action-stalks}.
Then the identification
$$
(R^j\alpha_*\mathcal{F})_{\Spec(\bar k)} \cong H^j (X_{\bar k},
\mathcal{F}|_{X_{\bar k}})
$$
from
\'Etale Cohomology, Theorem \ref{etale-cohomology-theorem-higher-direct-images}
is an isomorphism of $G_k$-modules.

nodes.title: Arithmetic frobenius
Geometric arithmetic inverse
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03SV}}


Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_\etale$. Then for all
$j\geq 0$, $\text{frob}_k$ acts on the cohomology group $H^j(X_{\bar k},
\mathcal{F}|_{X_{\bar k}})$ as the inverse of the map $\pi_X^*$.

nodes.title: Geometric frobenius on stalk
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03SW}}


If $x \in X(k)$ is a rational point and $\bar x : \Spec(\bar k) \to X$
the geometric point lying over $x$, we let $\pi_x : \mathcal{F}_{\bar x} \to
\mathcal{F}_{\bar x}$ denote the action by $\text{frob}_k^{-1}$ and call it the
{\it geometric frobenius}\footnote{This notation is not standard.
This operator is denoted $F_x$ in \cite{SGA4.5}. We will likely change
this notation in the future.}

nodes.title: Trace
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03T0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03T0}}


The {\it trace} of the endomorphism $a$ is the sum of the diagonal entries of
a matrix representing it. This defines an additive map $\text{Tr} :
\text{End}_\Lambda(\Lambda^{\oplus m}) \to \Lambda^\natural$.

nodes.title: When in bounded
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03T5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03T5}}


An object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{A})$ is contained in $D^+(\mathcal{A})$ if and
only if $H^i(E) =0 $ for all $i \ll 0$. Similar statements hold for $D^-$ and
$D^b$.

nodes.title: Derived categories
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03T6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03T6}}


Morphisms between objects in the derived category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Let $I^\bullet \in \text{Comp}^+(\mathcal{A})$ with $I^n$ injective for all
$n \in \mathbf{Z}$. Then
$$
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{A})}(K^\bullet, I^\bullet)
=
\Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(K^\bullet, I^\bullet).
$$
\item
Let $P^\bullet \in \text{Comp}^-(\mathcal{A})$ with $P^n$ is projective for all
$n \in \mathbf{Z}$. Then
$$
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{A})}(P^\bullet, K^\bullet)
=
\Hom_{K(\mathcal{A})}(P^\bullet, K^\bullet).
$$
\item
If $\mathcal{A}$ has enough injectives and $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{A}$
is the additive subcategory of injectives, then
$
D^+(\mathcal{A})\cong K^+(\mathcal{I})
$
(as triangulated categories).
\item
If $\mathcal{A}$ has enough projectives and $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathcal{A}$
is the additive subcategory of projectives, then
$
D^-(\mathcal{A}) \cong K^-(\mathcal{P}).
$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Derived functor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03T7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03T7}}


Let $F: \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a left exact functor and assume that
$\mathcal{A}$ has enough injectives. We define the {\it total right derived
functor of $F$} as the functor $RF: D^+(\mathcal{A}) \to D^+(\mathcal{B})$
fitting into the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}D^+(\mathcal{A}) \overset{RF}{\longrightarrow} & D^+(\mathcal{B}) \\ K^+(\mathcal I) \uparrow\overset{F}{\longrightarrow} & K^+(\mathcal{B}). \uparrow\end{array}
$$
This is possible since the left vertical arrow is invertible by the previous
lemma. Similarly, let $G: \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a right exact
functor and assume that $\mathcal{A}$ has enough projectives. We define the
{\it total left derived functor of $G$} as the functor $LG: D^-(\mathcal{A})
\to D^-(\mathcal{B})$ fitting into the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}D^-(\mathcal{A}) \overset{LG}{\longrightarrow} & D^-(\mathcal{B}) \\ K^-(\mathcal{P}) \uparrow\overset{G}{\longrightarrow} & K^-(\mathcal{B}). \uparrow\end{array}
$$
This is possible since the left vertical arrow is invertible by the previous
lemma.

nodes.title: Filtered
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TA}}


Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$ be the category of filtered objects
$(A, F)$ of $\mathcal{A}$, where $F$ is a filtration of the form
$$
A \supset \ldots \supset F^n A \supset F^{n+1}A \supset \ldots
\supset 0.
$$
This is an additive category.
\item We denote $\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$ the full
subcategory of $\text{Fil}(\mathcal{A})$ whose objects $(A, F)$ have finite
filtration. This is also an additive category.
\item An object $I \in \text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$ is called
{\it filtered injective} (respectively {\it projective}) provided
that $\text{gr}^p(I) = \text{gr}_F^p(I) = F^pI/F^{p+1}I$ is injective
(resp. projective) in $\mathcal{A}$ for all $p$.
\item The category of complexes
$\text{Comp}(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})) \supset
\text{Comp}^+(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$
and its homotopy category
$K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})) \supset K^+(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal A))$
are defined as before.
\item A morphism $\alpha : K^\bullet \to L^\bullet$ of complexes in
$\text{Comp}(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$ is called a
{\it filtered quasi-isomorphism} provided that
$$
\text{gr}^p(\alpha): \text{gr}^p(K^\bullet) \to \text{gr}^p(L^\bullet)
$$
is a quasi-isomorphism for all $p \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\item We define $DF(\mathcal{A})$ (resp. $DF^+(\mathcal{A})$)
by inverting the filtered quasi-isomorphisms in
$K(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$ (resp. $K^+(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A}))$).
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Filtered derived category
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TB}}


If $\mathcal{A}$ has enough injectives, then $DF^+(\mathcal{A}) \cong
K^+(\mathcal{I})$, where $\mathcal{I}$ is the full additive subcategory of
$\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$ consisting of filtered injective objects.
Similarly, if $\mathcal{A}$ has enough projectives, then $DF^-(\mathcal{A})
\cong K^-(\mathcal{P})$, where $\mathcal P$ is the full additive subcategory of
$\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{A})$ consisting of filtered projective objects.

nodes.title: Filtered derived functors
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TD}}


Let $T: \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a left exact functor and assume that
$\mathcal{A}$ has enough injectives. Define $RT: DF^+(\mathcal{A}) \to D
F^+(\mathcal{B})$ to fit in the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}DF^+(\mathcal{A}) \overset{RT}{\longrightarrow} & DF^+(\mathcal{B}) \\ K^+(\mathcal{I}) \uparrow\overset{T \quad}{\longrightarrow} & K^+(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{B})).
\uparrow\end{array}
$$
This is well-defined by the previous lemma. Let $G: \mathcal{A} \to
\mathcal{B}$ be a right exact functor and assume that $\mathcal{A}$ has enough
projectives. Define $LG: DF^-(\mathcal{A}) \to DF^-(\mathcal{B})$ to fit in
the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}DF^-(\mathcal{A}) \overset{LG}{\longrightarrow} & DF^-(\mathcal{B}) \\ K^-(\mathcal{P}) \uparrow\overset{G \quad}{\longrightarrow} & K^-(\text{Fil}^f(\mathcal{B})).
\uparrow\end{array}
$$
Again, this is well-defined by the previous lemma.
The functors $RT$, resp.\ $LG$, are called the {\it filtered derived
functor} of $T$, resp.\ $G$.

nodes.title: Compare filtered graded
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TE}}


In the situation above, we have
$$
\text{gr}^p \circ RT = RT \circ \text{gr}^p
$$
where the $RT$ on the left is the filtered derived functor while the one on the
right is the total derived functor. That is, there is a commuting diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}DF^+(\mathcal{A}) \overset{RT}{\longrightarrow}\underset{\text{gr}^p}{\downarrow} & DF^+(\mathcal{B})
\overset{\text{gr}^p}{\downarrow} \\ D^+(\mathcal{A}) \overset{RT}{\longrightarrow} & D^+(\mathcal{B}).\end{array}
$$

nodes.title: Perfect
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TH}}


We denote by $K_{perf}(\Lambda)$ the category whose objects are bounded
complexes of finite projective $\Lambda$-modules, and whose morphisms are
morphisms of complexes up to homotopy. The functor $K_{perf}(\Lambda)\to
D(\Lambda)$ is fully faithful (Derived Categories, Lemma
\ref{derived-lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex}).
Denote $D_{perf}(\Lambda)$ its essential image.
An object of $D(\Lambda)$ is called {\it perfect} if it is in
$D_{perf}(\Lambda)$.

nodes.title: Trace well defined
Additivity
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TK}}


Let $K\in DF_{\text{perf}}(\Lambda)$ and $f\in
\text{End}_{DF}(K)$. Then
$$
\text{Tr}(f|_K) =
\sum\nolimits_{p\in \mathbf{Z}} \text{Tr}(f|_{\text{gr}^p K}).
$$

nodes.title: Additive filtered finite projective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TL}}


Let $P \in \text{Fil}^f(\text{Mod}_\Lambda)$ be filtered finite projective, and
$f : P \to P$ an endomorphism in $\text{Fil}^f(\text{Mod}_\Lambda)$. Then
$$
\text{Tr}(f|_P) =
\sum\nolimits_p \text{Tr}(f|_{\text{gr}^p(P)}).
$$

nodes.title: Finite tor dimension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TN}}


Let $\Lambda$ be a (possibly noncommutative) ring.
An object $K\in D(\Lambda)$ has {\it finite $\text{Tor}$-dimension}
if there exist $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$ such that for any
right $\Lambda$-module $N$, we have
$H^i(N \otimes_{\Lambda}^\mathbf{L} K) = 0$ for all
$i \not \in [a, b]$.

nodes.title: Characterize perfect
Projective curve constructible cohomology
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TV}}


Let $X$ be a projective curve over a field $k$, $\Lambda$ a finite ring and
$K\in D_{ctf}(X, \Lambda)$. Then $R\Gamma(X_{\bar k}, K)\in
D_{perf}(\Lambda)$.

nodes.title: Global lefschetz number
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TX}}


Let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring, $X$ a projective curve over a finite field $k$
and $K \in D_{ctf}(X, \Lambda)$ (for instance $K = \underline\Lambda$).
There is a canonical map $c_K : \pi_X^{-1}K \to K$, and its base change
$c_K|_{X_{\bar k}}$ induces an action denoted $\pi_X^*$ on the perfect
complex $R\Gamma(X_{\bar k}, K|_{X_{\bar k}})$. The
{\it global Lefschetz number} of $K$ is the trace
$\text{Tr}(\pi_X^* |_{R\Gamma(X_{\bar k}, K)})$ of that action.
It is an element of $\Lambda^\natural$.

nodes.title: Local lefschetz number
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03TY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03TY}}



With $\Lambda, X, k, K$ as in
Definition \ref{trace-definition-global-lefschetz-number}.
Since $K\in D_{ctf}(X, \Lambda)$, for any geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$,
the complex $K_{\bar x}$ is a perfect complex (in $D_{perf}(\Lambda)$). As we
have seen in Section \ref{trace-section-frobenii}, the Frobenius $\pi_X$ acts on
$K_{\bar x}$. The {\it local Lefschetz number} of $K$ is the sum
$$
\sum\nolimits_{x\in X(k)} \text{Tr}(\pi_x |_{K_{\overline{x}}})
$$
which is again an element of $\Lambda^\natural$.

nodes.title: Lefschetz Trace Formula
Weil
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03U1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03U1}}


Let $C$ be a nonsingular projective curve over an algebraically closed field
$k$, and $\varphi : C \to C$ a $k$-endomorphism of $C$ distinct from the
identity. Let $V(\varphi) = \Delta_C \cdot \Gamma_\varphi$, where $\Delta_C$ is
the diagonal, $\Gamma_\varphi$ is the graph of $\varphi$, and the intersection
number is taken on $C \times C$. Let $J = \underline{\Picardfunctor}^0_{C/k}$
be the jacobian of $C$ and denote $\varphi^* : J \to J$ the action induced by
$\varphi$ by taking pullbacks. Then
$$
V(\varphi) = 1 - \text{Tr}_J(\varphi^*) + \deg \varphi.
$$

nodes.title: Weil mod
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03U3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03U3}}



Consider the situation of
Theorem \ref{trace-theorem-weil-trace-formula}
and let $\ell$ be a prime number invertible in $k$. Then
$$
\sum\nolimits_{i = 0}^2
(-1)^i
\text{Tr}(\varphi^* |_{H^i (C, \underline{\mathbf{Z}/\ell^n \mathbf{Z}})})
=
V(\varphi) \mod \ell^n.
$$

nodes.title: Epsilon
Trace G
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03U6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03U6}}


Let $f : P\to P$ be an
endomorphism of a finite projective $\Lambda[G]$-module
$P$. We define
$$
\text{Tr}_{\Lambda}^G(f; P) := \varepsilon\left(\text{Tr}_{\Lambda[G]}(f;
P)\right)
$$
to be the {\it $G$-trace of $f$ on $P$}.

nodes.title: Lambda trace
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03U7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03U7}}


Let $f : P\to P$ be an endomorphism of the finite projective
$\Lambda[G]$-module $P$. Then
$$
\text{Tr}_{\Lambda}(f; P) = \# G \cdot \text{Tr}_\Lambda^G(f; P).
$$

nodes.title: A module structure
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03U8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03U8}}


The map $A\to \Lambda$ defines an $A$-module structure on $\Lambda^\natural$.

nodes.title: Diagonal action projective module
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03U9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03U9}}


Let $P$ be a finite projective $A[G]$-module and $M$ a $\Lambda[G]$-module,
finite projective as a $\Lambda$-module. Then $P \otimes_A M$ is a finite
projective $\Lambda[G]$-module, for the structure induced by the diagonal
action of $G$.

nodes.title: Multiplicative trace
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UA}}



With assumptions as in
Lemma \ref{trace-lemma-diagonal-action-projective-module},
let
$u\in \text{End}_{A[G]}(P)$ and $v\in \text{End}_{\Lambda[G]}(M)$. Then
$$
\text{Tr}_\Lambda^G \left(u \otimes v; P \otimes_A M\right) = \text{Tr}_A^G(u;
P)\cdot \text{Tr}_\Lambda(v;M).
$$

nodes.title: Gamma z gamma trace
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UB}}


Let $P$ be a $\Lambda[\Gamma]$-module, finite and projective as a
$\Lambda[G]$-module, and $\gamma \in \Gamma$. Then
$$
\text{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\gamma, P) =
\# Z_\gamma \cdot \text{Tr}_\Lambda^{Z_\gamma}\left(\gamma, P\right).
$$

nodes.title: Weak trace
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UC}}


Let $P$ be an $A[\Gamma]$-module, finite projective as $A[G]$-module. Let $M$
be a $\Lambda[\Gamma]$-module, finite projective as a $\Lambda$-module. Then
$$
\text{Tr}_{\Lambda}^{Z_\gamma}(\gamma, P \otimes_A M) =
\text{Tr}_A^{Z_\gamma}(\gamma, P)\cdot \text{Tr}_\Lambda(\gamma, M).
$$

nodes.title: Trivial trace
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UD}}


Let $P$ be a $\Lambda[\Gamma]$-module, finite projective as
$\Lambda[G]$-module. Then the coinvariants
$P_G = \Lambda \otimes_{\Lambda[G]} P$
form a finite projective $\Lambda$-module, endowed with an action of
$\Gamma/G = \mathbf{N}$. Moreover, we have
$$
\text{Tr}_\Lambda(1; P_G) =
\sum\nolimits'_{\gamma \mapsto 1} \text{Tr}_\Lambda^{Z_\gamma}(\gamma, P)
$$
where $\sum_{\gamma\mapsto 1}'$ means taking the sum over the $G$-conjugacy
classes in $\Gamma$.

nodes.title: Trace formula again
L adic sheaf
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UM}}


Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. A {\it $\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaf} on $X$, or
simply an {\it $\ell$-adic sheaf} $\mathcal{F}$ is an
inverse system $\left\{\mathcal{F}_n\right\}_{n\geq 1}$ where
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\mathcal{F}_n$ is a constructible $\mathbf{Z}/\ell^n\mathbf{Z}$-module on
$X_\etale$, and
\item
the transition maps $\mathcal{F}_{n+1}\to \mathcal{F}_n$ induce isomorphisms
$\mathcal{F}_{n+1} \otimes_{\mathbf{Z}/\ell^{n+1}\mathbf{Z}}
\mathbf{Z}/\ell^n\mathbf{Z} \cong \mathcal{F}_n$.
\end{enumerate}
We say that $\mathcal{F}$ is {\it lisse} if each $\mathcal{F}_n$ is locally
constant. A {\it morphism} of such is merely a morphism of inverse systems.

nodes.title: Eventually constant
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UN}}


Let $\{\mathcal{G}_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ be an inverse system of constructible
$\mathbf{Z}/\ell^n\mathbf{Z}$-modules.
Suppose that for all $k\geq 1$, the maps
$$
\mathcal{G}_{n+1}/\ell^k \mathcal{G}_{n+1}\to \mathcal{G}_n /\ell^k
\mathcal{G}_n
$$
are isomorphisms for all $n\gg 0$ (where the bound possibly depends on $k$).
In other words, assume that the system
$\{\mathcal{G}_n/\ell^k\mathcal{G}_n\}_{n\geq 1}$
is eventually constant, and call $\mathcal{F}_k$ the corresponding sheaf.
Then the system $\left\{\mathcal{F}_k\right\}_{k\geq 1}$ forms a
$\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaf on $X$.

nodes.title: L adic abelian
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UO}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UO}}


The category of $\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaves on $X$ is abelian.

nodes.title: Torsion l adic sheaf
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UR}}


A $\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is {\it torsion} if
$\ell^n : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$ is the zero map for some $n$.
The abelian category
of $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-sheaves on $X$ is the quotient of the abelian category of
$\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaves by the Serre subcategory of torsion sheaves. In
other words, its objects are $\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaves on $X$, and if
$\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ are two such, then
$$
\Hom_{\mathbf{Q}_\ell} \left(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G} \right) =
\Hom_{\mathbf{Z}_\ell} \left(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}\right)
\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}_\ell} \mathbf{Q}_\ell.
$$
We denote by $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathbf{Q}_\ell$ the
quotient functor (right adjoint to the inclusion). If $\mathcal{F} =
\mathcal{F}' \otimes \mathbf{Q}_\ell$ where $\mathcal{F}'$ is a
$\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaf and $\bar x$ is a geometric point, then the
{\it stalk} of $\mathcal{F}$ at $\bar x$ is $\mathcal{F}_{\bar x} =
\mathcal{F}'_{\bar x} \otimes \mathbf{Q}_\ell$.

nodes.title: Cohomology l adic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UT}}


If $X$ is a separated scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field
$k$ and $\mathcal{F} = \left\{\mathcal{F}_n\right\}_{n\geq 1}$ is a
$\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaf on $X$, then we define
$$
H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) := \lim_n H^i(X, \mathcal{F}_n)
\quad\text{and}\quad
H_c^i(X, \mathcal{F}) := \lim_n H_c^i(X, \mathcal{F}_n).
$$
If $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}'\otimes \mathbf{Q}_\ell$ for a
$\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-sheaf $\mathcal{F}'$ then we set
$$
H_c^i(X , \mathcal{F}) := H_c^i(X,
\mathcal{F}')\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}_\ell}\mathbf{Q}_\ell.
$$
We call these the {\it $\ell$-adic cohomology} of $X$ with coefficients
$\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.title: L function finite ring
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UV}}


Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a finite field $k$. Let $\Lambda$ be a
finite ring of order prime to the characteristic of $k$ and $\mathcal{F}$ a
constructible flat $\Lambda$-module on $X_\etale$. Then we set
$$
L(X, \mathcal{F}) :=
\prod\nolimits_{x\in |X|}
\det(1 - \pi_x^*T^{\deg x} |_{\mathcal{F}_{\bar x}})^{-1} \in \Lambda [[ T ]]
$$
where $|X|$ is the set of closed points of $X$, $\deg x = [\kappa(x): k]$ and
$\bar x$ is a geometric point lying over $x$. This definition clearly
generalizes to the case where $\mathcal{F}$ is replaced by a
$K \in D_{ctf}(X, \Lambda)$. We call this the {\it $L$-function of
$\mathcal{F}$}.

nodes.title: L function l adic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UX}}


Now assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is a $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $X$.
In this case we define
$$
L(X, \mathcal{F}) :=
\prod\nolimits_{x \in |X|}
\det(1 - \pi_x^*T^{\deg x} |_{\mathcal{F}_{\bar x}})^{-1}
\in \mathbf{Q}_\ell[[T]].
$$
Note that this product converges since there are finitely many points of a
given degree. We call this the {\it $L$-function of
$\mathcal{F}$}.

nodes.title: Finite Coefficients
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03UZ}}


Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a finite field $k$. Let $\Lambda$ be a
finite ring of order prime to the characteristic of $k$ and $\mathcal{F}$ a
constructible flat $\Lambda$-module on $X_\etale$. Then
$$
L(X, \mathcal{F}) =
\det(1 - \pi_X^*\ T |_{R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar k}, \mathcal{F})})^{-1}
\in \Lambda[[T]].
$$

nodes.title: Adic sheaves
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03V0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03V0}}


Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a finite field $k$, and $\mathcal{F}$ a
$\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $X$. Then
$$
L(X, \mathcal{F}) =
\prod\nolimits_i
\det(1 - \pi_X^*T |_{H_c^i(X_{\bar k} , \mathcal{F})})^{(-1)^{i + 1}}
\in \mathbf{Q}_\ell[[T]].
$$

nodes.title: D
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03V3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03V3}}


Let $X/k$ be as above, let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring with $\#\Lambda \in k^*$
and $K\in D_{ctf}(X, \Lambda)$. Then $R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar k}, K)\in
D_{perf}(\Lambda)$ and
$$
\sum_{x\in X(k)}\text{Tr}\left(\pi_x |_{K_{\bar x}}\right) =
\text{Tr}\left(\pi_X^* |_{R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar k}, K )}\right).
$$

nodes.title: C
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03V2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03V2}}


Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over a finite field $k$ and
$\mathcal{F}$ be a $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $X$. Then
$\dim_{\mathbf{Q}_\ell}H_c^i(X_{\bar k}, \mathcal{F})$ is finite for all $i$,
and is nonzero for $0\leq i \leq 2 \dim X$ only. Furthermore, we have
$$
\sum_{x\in X(k)} \text{Tr}\left(\pi_x |_{\mathcal{F}_{\bar x}}\right) =
\sum_i (-1)^i\text{Tr}\left(\pi_X^* |_{H_c^i(X_{\bar k}, \mathcal{F})}\right).
$$

nodes.title: Piece together
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03V4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03V4}}


Suppose we have
$K_n\in D_{perf}(\mathbf{Z}/\ell^n\mathbf{Z})$, $\pi_n : K_n\to K_n$
and isomorphisms
$\varphi_n :
K_{n+1} \otimes^\mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{Z}/\ell^{n+1}\mathbf{Z}}
\mathbf{Z}/\ell^n\mathbf{Z}
\to K_n$
compatible with $\pi_{n+1}$ and $\pi_n$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the elements $t_n = \text{Tr}(\pi_n |_{K_n})\in \mathbf{Z}/\ell^n\mathbf{Z}$
form an element $t_\infty = \{t_n\}$ of $\mathbf{Z}_\ell$,
\item
the $\mathbf{Z}_\ell$-module $H_\infty^i = \lim_n H^i(k_n)$ is finite and
is nonzero for finitely many $i$ only, and
\item
the operators $H^i(\pi_n): H^i(K_n)\to H^i(K_n)$ are compatible and define
$\pi_\infty^i : H_\infty^i\to H_\infty^i$ satisfying
$$
\sum (-1)^i \text{Tr}(
\pi_\infty^i |_{H_\infty^i \otimes_{\mathbf{Z}_\ell}\mathbf{Q}_\ell}) =
t_\infty.
$$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Count points projective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03V8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03V8}}


Let $X$ be a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible
curve over a finite field $k$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the $L$-function $L(X, \mathbf{Q}_\ell)$ is a rational function,
\item the eigenvalues $\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_{2g}$ of $\pi_X^*$ on
$H^1(X_{\bar k}, \mathbf{Q}_\ell)$ are algebraic integers
independent of $\ell$,
\item the number of rational points of $X$ on $k_n$, where $[k_n : k] = n$, is
$$
\# X(k_n) = 1 - \sum\nolimits_{i = 1}^{2g}\alpha_i^n + q^n,
$$
\item for each $i$, $|\alpha_i| < q$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Open
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VE}}


A subgroup of the form
$\text{Stab}(\overline y\in F_{\overline{x}}(Y))\subset \pi_1(X, \overline{x})$
is called {\it open}.

nodes.title: Grothendieck
Integral normal fundamental group
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VG}}


Let $X$ be an integral normal Noetherian scheme. Let
$\overline y\to X$ be an algebraic geometric point lying
over the generic point $\eta\in X$. Then
$$
\pi_x(X, \overline \eta) = Gal(M/\kappa(\eta))
$$
($\kappa(\eta)$, function field of $X$) where
$$
\kappa(\overline \eta)\supset M\supset \kappa(\eta) = k(X)
$$
is the max sub-extension such that for every finite sub extension
$M\supset L\supset \kappa(\eta)$ the normalization of $X$ in $L$ is finite
\'etale over $X$.

nodes.title: Deligne, Weil II
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VH}}


For a sheaf
$\mathcal{F}_\rho$ with $\rho$ satisfying the conclusions of the conjecture
above then the eigenvalues of $\pi_X^*$ on $H_c^i(X_{\overline{k}},
\mathcal{F}_{\rho})$ are algebraic numbers $\alpha$ with absolute values
$$
|\alpha|=q^{w/2}, \text{ for }w\in \mathbf{Z},\ w\leq i
$$
Moreover, if $X$ smooth and proj. then $w = i$.

nodes.title: Identify h2c
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VK}}


There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
H_c^2(X_{\overline{k}}, \mathcal{F}_\rho)=(M)_{\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}},
\overline\eta)}(-1)
$$
as $\text{Gal}(k^{^{sep}}/k)$-modules.

nodes.title: Curve kpi1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VM}}


Let $X/k$ as before but $X_{\overline{k}}\neq \mathbf{P}^1_{\overline{k}}$
The functors
$
(M, \rho)\mapsto H_c^{2-i}(X_{\overline{k}}, \mathcal{F}_\rho)
$
are the left derived functor of
$(M, \rho)\mapsto H_c^2(X_{\overline{k}}, \mathcal{F}_\rho)$
so
$$
H_c^{2-i}(X_{\overline{k}}, \mathcal{F}_\rho) =
H_i(\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}}, \overline \eta), M)(-1)
$$
Moreover, there is a derived version, namely
$$
R\Gamma_c(X_{\overline{k}}, \mathcal{F}_\rho)
=
LH_0(\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}}, \overline \eta), M(-1))
=
M(-1)
\otimes_{\Lambda[[\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}}, \overline \eta)]]}^\mathbf{L}
\Lambda
$$
in $D(\Lambda[[\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}]])$.
Similarly, the functors
$(M, \rho)\mapsto H^i(X_{\overline{k}}, \mathcal{F}_\rho)$
are the right derived functor of
$(M, \rho)\mapsto M^{\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}}, \overline \eta)}$
so
$$
H^i(X_{\overline{k}}, \mathcal{F}_\rho) =
H^i(\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}}, \overline \eta), M)
$$
Moreover, in this case there is a derived version too.

nodes.title: Unramified
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VS}}


An {\it unramified cusp form on $\text{GL}_2(\mathbf{A})$ with values in
$\Lambda$}\footnote{This is likely nonstandard notation.}
is a function
$$
f : \text{GL}_2(\mathbf{A}) \to \Lambda
$$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f(x\gamma) = f(x)$ for all $x\in \text{GL}_2(\mathbf{A})$ and all
$\gamma\in \text{GL}_2(K)$
\item $f(ux) = f(x)$ for all $x\in \text{GL}_2(\mathbf{A})$ and all
$u\in \text{GL}_2(O)$
\item for all $x\in \text{GL}_2(\mathbf{A})$,
$$
\int_{\mathbf{A} \mod K} f
\left(x
\left(
\begin{matrix}
1 & z \\
0 & 1
\end{matrix}
\right)
\right) dz = 0
$$
see \cite[Section 4.1]{dJ-conjecture}
for an explanation of how to make sense out
of this for a general ring $\Lambda$ in which $p$ is invertible.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Drinfeld make rho
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VT}}


Given an eigenform $f$ with values in
$\overline{\mathbf{Q}}_l$ and eigenvalues
$u_v\in \overline{\mathbf{Z}}_l^*$ then there exists
$$
\rho : \pi_1(X)\to \text{GL}_2(E)
$$
continuous, absolutely irreducible where
$E$ is a finite extension of $\mathbf{Q}_\ell$ contained in
$\overline{\mathbf{Q}}_l$ such that
$t_v = \text{Tr}(\rho(F_v))$, and
$u_v = q_v^{-1}\det\left(\rho(F_v)\right)$ for all places $v$.

nodes.title: Drinfeld make f
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VU}}


Suppose $\mathbf{Q}_l \subset E$ finite, and
$$
\rho : \pi_1(X)\to \text{GL}_2(E)
$$
absolutely irreducible, continuous. Then there exists an eigenform $f$ with
values in $\overline{\mathbf{Q}}_l$ whose eigenvalues $t_v$, $u_v$
satisfy the equalities
$t_v = \text{Tr}(\rho(F_v))$ and $u_v = q_v^{-1}\det(\rho(F_v))$.

nodes.title: Cusp forms finite
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VW}}


If $\Lambda$ is Noetherian then $C(\Lambda)$ is a
finitely generated $\Lambda$-module. Moreover, if $\Lambda$ is a field with
prime subfield $\mathbf{F} \subset \Lambda$ then
$$
C(\Lambda)=(C(\mathbf{F}))\otimes_{\mathbf{F}}\Lambda
$$
compatibly with $T_v$ acting.

nodes.title: Eigenvalues algebraic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VX}}


Algebraicity of eigenvalues.
If $\Lambda$ is a field then the eigenvalues $t_v$ for $f\in
C(\Lambda)$ are algebraic over the prime subfield
$\mathbf{F} \subset \Lambda$.

nodes.title: Switch l
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VY}}


Switching $l$. Let $E$ be a number field.
Start with
$$
\rho : \pi_1(X)\to SL_2(E_\lambda)
$$
absolutely irreducible continuous, where $\lambda$ is a place of $E$
not lying above $p$. Then for any second place $\lambda'$ of $E$
not lying above $p$ there exists a finite extension $E'_{\lambda'}$
and a absolutely irreducible continuous representation
$$
\rho': \pi_1(X)\to SL_2(E'_{\lambda'})
$$
which is compatible with $\rho$ in the sense that the characteristic
polynomials of all Frobenii are the same.

nodes.title: Conjecture n 2
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03VZ}}


The Conjecture holds if $n\leq 2$.

nodes.title: Conjecture l bigger 2n
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03W0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03W0}}


Conjecture holds if $l > 2n$ modulo some unproven things.

nodes.title: Deformation rings
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03W1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03W1}}


(See \cite[Theorem 3.5]{dJ-conjecture})
Suppose
$$
\rho_0: \pi_1(X)\to \text{GL}_n(\mathbf{F}_l)
$$
is a continuous, $l\neq p$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item Conj. holds for $X$,
\item $\rho_0 |_{\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}})}$ abs. irred., and
\item $l$ does not divide $n$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the universal deformation ring $R_{\text{univ}}$ of $\rho_0$ is
finite flat over $\mathbf{Z}_l$.

nodes.title: Finite set frobenii generate topologically
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03W5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03W5}}


There exists a finite set $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ of closed points of $X$
such that set of {\bf all} frobenius elements corresponding to these
points topologically generate $\pi_1(X)$.

nodes.title: Composition correspondences
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FG0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FG0}}


We have the following for correspondences:
\begin{enumerate}
\item composition of correspondences is $\mathbf{Q}$-bilinear
and associative,
\item there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\CH_{-r}(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q} = \text{Corr}^r(X, \Spec(k))
$$
such that pullback by correspondences corresponds to composition,
\item there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\CH^r(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q} = \text{Corr}^r(\Spec(k), X)
$$
such that pushforward by correspondences corresponds to composition,
\item composition of correspondences is compatible with pushforward and
pullback of cycles.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Category correspondences
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FG2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FG2}}


Smooth projective schemes over $k$ with correspondences and composition
of correspondences as defined above form a graded category over
$\mathbf{Q}$
(Differential Graded Algebra, Definition \ref{dga-definition-graded-category}).

nodes.title: Contravariant functor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FG3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FG3}}


There is a contravariant functor from the category of smooth
projective schemes over $k$ to the category of correspondences
which is the identity on objects and sends $f : Y \to X$ to
the element $[\Gamma_f] \in \text{Corr}^0(X, Y)$.

nodes.title: Functor and cycles
Tensor product
Prep dual
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FG8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FG8}}


Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of smooth projective schemes over $k$.
Assume $X$ and $Y$ equidimensional of dimensions $d$ and $e$.
Denote $a = [\Gamma_f] \in \text{Corr}^0(X, Y)$ and
$a^t = [\Gamma_f^t] \in \text{Corr}^{d - e}(Y, X)$.
Set
$\eta_X = [\Gamma_{X \to X \times X}] \in \text{Corr}^0(X \times X, X)$,
$\eta_Y = [\Gamma_{Y \to Y \times Y}] \in \text{Corr}^0(Y \times Y, Y)$,
$[X] \in \text{Corr}^{-d}(X, \Spec(k))$, and
$[Y] \in \text{Corr}^{-e}(Y, \Spec(k))$. The diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}X \otimes Y \underset{a \otimes \text{id}}{\longrightarrow}\underset{\text{id} \otimes a^t}{\downarrow} & Y \otimes Y \underset{\eta_Y}{\longrightarrow} & Y \overset{[Y]}{\downarrow} \\ X \otimes X \overset{\eta_X}{\longrightarrow} & X \overset{[X]}{\longrightarrow} & \Spec(k)\end{array}
$$
is commutative in the category of correspondences.

nodes.title: Motives
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGA}}


The category $M_k$ whose objects are motives over $k$ and morphisms
are morphisms of motives over $k$ is a $\mathbf{Q}$-linear category.
There is a contravariant functor
$$
h : \{\text{smooth projective schemes over }k\} \longrightarrow M_k
$$
defined by $h(X) = (X, 1, 0)$ and $h(f) = [\Gamma_f]$.

nodes.title: Karoubian
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGB}}


The category $M_k$ is Karoubian.

nodes.title: Motives monoidal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGC}}


The category $M_k$ with tensor product defined as above
is symmetric monoidal with the obvious associativity and commutativity
constraints and with unit $\mathbf{1} = (\Spec(k), 1, 0)$.

nodes.title: Inverse h2
Additive
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGF}}


The category $M_k$ is additive.

nodes.title: Decompose P1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGG}}


In $M_k$ we have $h(\mathbf{P}^1_k) \cong \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathbf{1}(-1)$.

nodes.title: Characterize motives
Dual
Dual general
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGJ}}


Every object of $M_k$ has a left dual.

nodes.title: Chow group motives
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGL}}


Let $k$ be a base field. Let $M = (X, p, m)$ be a Chow motive over $k$.
For $i \in \mathbf{Z}$ we define the {\it $i$th Chow group of $M$}
by the formula
$$
\CH^i(M) = p\left(\CH^{i + m}(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q}\right)
$$

nodes.title: Chow groups representable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGM}}


Let $k$ be a base field. The functor $\CH^i(-)$ on the category
of motives $M_k$ is representable by $\mathbf{1}(-i)$, i.e., we
have
$$
\CH^i(M) = \Hom_{M_k}(\mathbf{1}(-i), M)
$$
functorially in $M$ in $M_k$.

nodes.title: Manin
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGN}}


Let $k$ be a base field. Let $c : M \to N$ be a morphism of motives.
If for every smooth projective scheme $X$ over $k$ the map
$c \otimes 1 : M \otimes h(X) \to N \otimes h(X)$ induces an isomorphism on
Chow groups, then $c$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Projective space bundle formula
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGQ}}


In the situation above, the map
$$
\sum\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, r - 1} c_i :
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, r - 1} h(X)(-i)
\longrightarrow
h(P)
$$
is an isomorphism in the category of motives.

nodes.title: Diagonal projective bundle
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGR}}



Let $p : P \to X$ be as in Lemma \ref{weil-lemma-projective-space-bundle-formula}.
The class $[\Delta_P]$ of the diagonal of $P$ in $\CH^*(P \times P)$
can be written
as
$$
[\Delta_P] =
\left(\sum\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, r - 1}
{r - 1 \choose i} c_{r - 1 - i}(\text{pr}_1^*\mathcal{S}^\vee) \cap
c_1(\text{pr}_2^*\mathcal{O}_P(1))^i\right)
\cap
(p \times p)^*[\Delta_X]
$$
where $\mathcal{S}$ is the kernel of the canonical surjection
$p^*\mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{O}_P(1)$.

nodes.title: Pushforward classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGT}}


Assume given (D1) and (D3) satisfying (A). For $f : X \to Y$
a morphism of smooth projective varieties we have
$f_*(f^*b \cup a) = b \cup f_*a$. If $g : Y \to Z$ is a second morphism
of smooth projective varieties, then $g_* \circ f_* = (g \circ f)_*$.

nodes.title: Weil cohomology theory classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGV}}


Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field.
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$.
A {\it classical Weil cohomology theory} over $k$ with coefficients in $F$
is given by data (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying
Poincar\'e duality, the K\"unneth formula, and compatibility
with cycle classes, more precisely, satisfying (A), (B), and (C).

nodes.title: Degrees cycles classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGW}}



Let $H^*$ be a classical Weil cohomology theory
(Definition \ref{weil-definition-weil-cohomology-theory-classical}).
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $d$. The diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\CH^d(X) \underset{\gamma}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow & H^{2d}(X) \overset{\int_X}{\downarrow} \\ \CH_0(X) \overset{\deg}{\longrightarrow} & F\end{array}
$$
commutes where $\deg : \CH_0(X) \to \mathbf{Z}$ is the degree of
zero cycles discussed in Chow Homology, Section
\ref{chow-section-degree-zero-cycles}.

nodes.title: Trace product classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGX}}



Let $H^*$ be a classical Weil cohomology theory
(Definition \ref{weil-definition-weil-cohomology-theory-classical}).
Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth projective varieties.
Then $\int_{X \times Y} = \int_X \otimes \int_Y$.

nodes.title: Pr2star classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGY}}



Let $H^*$ be a classical Weil cohomology theory
(Definition \ref{weil-definition-weil-cohomology-theory-classical}).
Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth projective varieties.
Then $\text{pr}_{2, *} : H^*(X \times Y) \to H^*(Y)$
sends $a \otimes b$ to $(\int_X a) b$.

nodes.title: Class diagonal classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FGZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FGZ}}



Let $H^*$ be a classical Weil cohomology theory
(Definition \ref{weil-definition-weil-cohomology-theory-classical}).
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $d$.
Choose a basis $e_{i, j}, j = 1, \ldots, \beta_i$ of $H^i(X)$ over $F$.
Using K\"unneth write
$$
\gamma([\Delta]) =
\sum\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, 2d}
\sum\nolimits_j e_{i, j} \otimes e'_{2d - i , j}
\quad\text{in}\quad
\bigoplus\nolimits_i H^i(X) \otimes_F H^{2d - i}(X)
$$
with $e'_{2d - i, j} \in H^{2d - i}(X)$.
Then $\int_X e_{i, j} \cup e'_{2d - i, j'} = (-1)^i\delta_{jj'}$.

nodes.title: Square diagonal classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FH0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FH0}}



Let $H^*$ be a classical Weil cohomology theory
(Definition \ref{weil-definition-weil-cohomology-theory-classical}).
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety. We have
$$
\sum\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, 2\dim(X)} (-1)^i\dim_F H^i(X) =
\deg([\Delta] \cdot [\Delta]) = \deg(c_d(\mathcal{T}_X) \cap [X])
$$

nodes.title: From functor to weil classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FH1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FH1}}


Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $F$ be a field of
characteristic $0$. Consider a $\mathbf{Q}$-linear functor
$$
G : M_k \longrightarrow \text{graded }F\text{-vector spaces}
$$
of symmetric monoidal categories such that $G(\mathbf{1}(1))$
is nonzero only in degree $-2$. Then we obtain data (D1), (D2), (D3)
satisfying all of (A), (B), (C) except for possibly (A)(c) and (A)(d).

nodes.title: From weil to functor classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FH2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FH2}}


Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $F$ be a field of
characteristic $0$. Let $H^*$ be a classical Weil cohomology theory.
Then we can construct a $\mathbf{Q}$-linear functor
$$
G : M_k \longrightarrow \text{graded }F\text{-vector spaces}
$$
of symmetric monoidal categories such that $H^*(X) = G(h(X))$.

nodes.title: Weil cohomology theory classical
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FH3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FH3}}


Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $F$ be a field of
characteristic $0$. A classical Weil cohomology theory is the same thing
as a $\mathbf{Q}$-linear functor
$$
G : M_k \longrightarrow \text{graded }F\text{-vector spaces}
$$
of symmetric monoidal categories together with an isomorphism
$F[2] \to G(\mathbf{1}(1))$ of graded $F$-vector spaces such that
in addition
\begin{enumerate}
\item $G(h(X))$ lives in nonnegative degrees, and
\item $\dim_F G^0(h(X)) = 1$
\end{enumerate}
for any smooth projective variety $X$.

nodes.title: Generated by separable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FH5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FH5}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $k$.
Then $\CH_0(X)$ is generated by classes of closed points whose residue
fields are separable over $k$.

nodes.title: Chow limit
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FH6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FH6}}


Let $K/k$ be an algebraic field extension. Let $X$ be a finite type
scheme over $k$. Then $\CH_i(X_K) = \colim \CH_i(X_{k'})$ where the
colimit is over the subextensions $K/k'/k$ with $k'/k$ finite.

nodes.title: Divide difference points
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FH7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FH7}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a geometrically irreducible
smooth projective scheme over $k$. Let $x, x' \in X$ be $k$-rational points.
Let $n$ be an integer invertible in $k$.
Then there exists a finite separable extension $k'/k$ such that
the pullback of $[x] - [x']$ to $X_{k'}$
is divisible by $n$ in $\CH_0(X_{k'})$.

nodes.title: Kernel to closure
Voevodsky
Pushforward
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHB}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), and (D3) satisfying (A). For $f : X \to Y$
a morphism of nonempty equidimensional smooth projective schemes over $k$
we have $f_*(f^*b \cup a) = b \cup f_*a$. If $g : Y \to Z$ is a second morphism
with $Z$ nonempty smooth projective and equidimensional, then
$g_* \circ f_* = (g \circ f)_*$.

nodes.title: Pr2star
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHC}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), and (D3) satisfying (A) and (B).
Let $X$ and $Y$ be nonempty smooth projective schemes over $k$
equidimensional of dimensions $d$ and $e$. Then
$\text{pr}_{2, *} : H^*(X \times Y)(d + e) \to H^*(Y)(e)$ sends
$a \otimes b$ to $(\int_X a) b$.

nodes.title: Base
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHE}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Then $H^i(\Spec(k)) = 0$ for $i \not = 0$ and there is a
unique $F$-algebra isomorphism $F = H^0(\Spec(k))$.
We have $\gamma([\Spec(k)]) = 1$ and $\int_{\Spec(k)} 1 = 1$.

nodes.title: Unit
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHF}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $k$.
If $X = \emptyset$, then $H^*(X) = 0$.
If $X$ is nonempty, then $\gamma([X]) = 1$ and $1 \not = 0$ in $H^0(X)$.

nodes.title: Push unit
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHG}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHG}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $i : X \to Y$ be a closed immersion of nonempty smooth projective
equidimensional schemes over $k$. Then
$\gamma([X]) = i_*1$ in $H^{2c}(Y)(c)$ where $c = \dim(Y) - \dim(X)$.

nodes.title: Class diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHH}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth projective scheme over $k$ equidimensional
of dimension $d$. Choose a basis $e_{i, j}, j = 1, \ldots, \beta_i$ of
$H^i(X)$ over $F$. Using K\"unneth write
$$
\gamma([\Delta]) =
\sum\nolimits_i
\sum\nolimits_j e_{i, j} \otimes e'_{2d - i , j}
\quad\text{in}\quad
\bigoplus\nolimits_i H^i(X) \otimes_F H^{2d - i}(X)(d)
$$
with $e'_{2d - i, j} \in H^{2d - i}(X)(d)$.
Then $\int_X e_{i, j} \cup e'_{2d - i, j'} = (-1)^i\delta_{jj'}$.

nodes.title: Cohomology P1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHI}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Then $H^*(\mathbf{P}^1_k)$ is $1$-dimensional in dimensions $0$ and $2$
and zero in other degrees.

nodes.title: Weil additive
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHJ}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
If $X$ and $Y$ are smooth projective schemes over $k$, then
$H^*(X \amalg Y) \to H^*(X) \times H^*(Y)$,
$a \mapsto (i^*a, j^*a)$ is an isomorphism where $i$, $j$
are the coprojections.

nodes.title: From functor to weil
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHK}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$.
Assume given a $\mathbf{Q}$-linear functor
$$
G : M_k \longrightarrow \text{graded }F\text{-vector spaces}
$$
of symmetric monoidal categories such that $G(\mathbf{1}(1))$
is nonzero only in degree $-2$. Then we obtain data (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3)
satisfying all of (A), (B), and (C) above.

nodes.title: From weil to functor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHL}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$. Given
(D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C)
we can construct a $\mathbf{Q}$-linear functor
$$
G : M_k \longrightarrow \text{graded }F\text{-vector spaces}
$$
of symmetric monoidal categories such that $H^*(X) = G(h(X))$.

nodes.title: Weil cohomology theory
Trace disjoint union
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHP}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $X, Y$ be nonempty smooth projective schemes both equidimensional
of dimension $d$ over $k$. Then $\int_{X \amalg Y} = \int_X + \int_Y$.

nodes.title: Dim 0
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHQ}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme of dimension zero over $k$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^i(X) = 0$ for $i \not = 0$,
\item $H^0(X)$ is a finite separable algebra over $F$,
\item $\dim_F H^0(X) = \deg(X \to \Spec(F))$,
\item $\int_X : H^0(X) \to F$ is the trace map,
\item $\gamma([X]) = 1$, and
\item $\int_X \gamma([X]) = \deg(X \to \Spec(k))$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Degrees cycles
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHR}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth projective scheme
equidimensional of dimension $d$ over $k$. The diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\CH^d(X) \underset{\gamma}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow & H^{2d}(X)(d) \overset{\int_X}{\downarrow} \\ \CH_0(X) \overset{\deg}{\longrightarrow} & F\end{array}
$$
commutes where $\deg : \CH_0(X) \to \mathbf{Z}$ is the degree of
zero cycles discussed in Chow Homology, Section
\ref{chow-section-degree-zero-cycles}.

nodes.title: Square diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHS}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth projective scheme over $k$ which is
equidimensional of dimension $d$. We have
$$
\sum\nolimits_i (-1)^i\dim_F H^i(X) =
\deg(\Delta \cdot \Delta) = \deg(c_d(\mathcal{T}_{X/k}))
$$

nodes.title: Algebra relations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHT}}


Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$.
Let $F'$ and $F_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$
be finite separable $F$-algebras. Let $A$ be a finite $F$-algebra.
Let $\sigma, \sigma' : A \to F'$ and $\sigma_i : A \to F_i$
be $F$-algebra maps. Assume $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ surjective.
If there is a relation
$$
\text{Tr}_{F'/F} \circ \sigma - \text{Tr}_{F'/F} \circ \sigma' =
n(\sum m_i \text{Tr}_{F_i/F} \circ \sigma_i)
$$
where $n > 1$ and $m_i$ are integers, then $\sigma = \sigma'$.

nodes.title: Relations classes points
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHU}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $k'/k$ be a finite separable extension.
Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $k'$.
Let $x, x' \in X$ be $k'$-rational points.
If $\gamma(x) \not = \gamma(x')$, then
$[x] - [x']$ is not divisible by any integer $n > 1$ in $\CH_0(X)$.

nodes.title: Classes points
