nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHV}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $k'/k$ be a finite separable extension. Let $X$ be a geometrically
irreducible smooth projective scheme over $k'$ of dimension $d$.
Then $\gamma : \CH_0(X) \to H^{2d}(X)(d)$ factors through
$\deg : \CH_0(X) \to \mathbf{Z}$.

nodes.title: Injective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHW}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C). Let
$f : X \to Y$ be a dominant morphism of irreducible smooth projective schemes
over $k$. Then $H^*(Y) \to H^*(X)$ is injective.

nodes.title: Otimes
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FHX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FHX}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C). Let
$k''/k'/k$ be finite separable algebras and let $X$ be a
smooth projective scheme over $k'$. Then
$$
H^*(X) \otimes_{H^0(\Spec(k'))} H^0(\Spec(k'')) =
H^*(X \times_{\Spec(k')} \Spec(k''))
$$

nodes.title: H 0 separable
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FI0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FI0}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $k$.
Set $k' = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exist finitely many closed points $x_1, \ldots, x_r \in X$
whose residue fields are separable over $k$ such that
$H^0(X) \to H^0(x_1) \oplus \ldots \oplus H^0(x_r)$ is injective,
\item the map $H^0(\Spec(k')) \to H^0(X)$ is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
If this is true, then $H^0(X)$ is a finite separable algebra over $F$.
If $X$ is equidimensional of dimension $d$, then (1) and (2)
are also equivalent to
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(3)] the classes of closed points generate $H^{2d}(X)(d)$
as a module over $H^0(X)$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Negative cohomology
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FI1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FI1}}



Assume given (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying (A), (B), and (C).
If there exists a smooth projective scheme $Y$ over $k$ such that
$H^i(Y)$ is nonzero for some $i < 0$, then there exists an equidimensional
smooth projective scheme $X$ over $k$ such that the equivalent conditions
of Lemma \ref{weil-lemma-H-0-separable} fail for $X$.

nodes.title: Weil cohomology theory
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FI2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FI2}}



Let $k$ be a field. Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$.
A {\it Weil cohomology theory} over $k$ with coefficients in $F$
is given by data (D0), (D1), (D2), and (D3) satisfying
Poincar\'e duality, the K\"unneth formula, and compatibility
with cycle classes, more precisely, satisfying axioms (A), (B), and (C)
of Section \ref{weil-section-axioms}
and in addition such that the equivalent conditions (1) and (2) of
Lemma \ref{weil-lemma-H-0-separable} hold for every smooth projective $X$ over $k$.

nodes.title: Weil cohomology theory again
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GIJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0GIJ}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$.
A Weil cohomology theory is the same thing as a $\mathbf{Q}$-linear
symmetric monoidal functor
$$
G : M_k \longrightarrow \text{graded }F\text{-vector spaces}
$$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $G(\mathbf{1}(1))$ is nonzero only in degree $-2$, and
\item for every smooth projective scheme $X$ over $k$ with
$k' = \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ the homomorphism
$G(h(\Spec(k'))) \to G(h(X))$ of graded $F$-vector spaces
is an isomorphism in degree $0$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Chern class
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FI5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FI5}}


In the situation above there is a unique rule which assigns to
every $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ a ``total Chern class''
$$
c^A : K_0(\textit{Vect}(X)) \longrightarrow  \prod\nolimits_{i \geq 0} A^i(X)
$$
with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ we have
$c^A(\alpha + \beta) = c^A(\alpha) c^A(\beta)$
and $c^A(0) = 1$.
\item If $f : X' \to X$ is a morphism of $\mathcal{C}$, then
$f^* \circ c^A =  c^A \circ f^*$.
\item Given $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and $\mathcal{L} \in \Pic(X)$
we have $c^A([\mathcal{L}]) = 1 + c_1^A(\mathcal{L})$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Splitting principle
Chern classes E tensor L
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FI8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FI8}}


Let $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a finite locally free
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then
$$
c^A_i({\mathcal E} \otimes {\mathcal L})
=
\sum\nolimits_{j = 0}^i
\binom{r - i + j}{j} c^A_{i - j}({\mathcal E}) \cup c^A_1({\mathcal L})^j
$$

nodes.title: Chern character
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FI9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FI9}}


In the situation above assume $A(X)$ is a $\mathbf{Q}$-algebra for all
$X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. Then there is a unique rule which assigns to
every $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ a ``chern character''
$$
ch^A : K_0(\textit{Vect}(X)) \longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \geq 0} A^i(X)
$$
with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $ch^A$ is a ring map for all $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
\item If $f : X' \to X$ is a morphism of $\mathcal{C}$, then
$f^* \circ ch^A =  ch^A \circ f^*$.
\item Given $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ and $\mathcal{L} \in \Pic(X)$
we have $ch^A([\mathcal{L}]) = \exp(c_1^A(\mathcal{L}))$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Adams and chern
Lambda operations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIC}}


Let $X$ be a scheme. There are maps
$$
\lambda^r : K_0(\textit{Vect}(X)) \longrightarrow K_0(\textit{Vect}(X))
$$
which sends $[\mathcal{E}]$ to $[\wedge^r(\mathcal{E})]$
when $\mathcal{E}$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
and which are compatible with pullbacks.

nodes.title: Chern classes
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIE}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1), (A2), (A3), and (A4).
There is a unique rule which assigns to every smooth projective $X$ over $k$
a ring homomorphism
$$
ch^H :
K_0(\textit{Vect}(X))
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \geq 0} H^{2i}(X)(i)
$$
compatible with pullbacks such that
$ch^H(\mathcal{L}) = \exp(c_1^H(\mathcal{L}))$
for any invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{L}$.

nodes.title: Cycle classes
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIF}}


Assume given (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1), (A2), (A3), and (A4).
There is a unique rule which assigns to every smooth projective $X$ over $k$
a graded ring homomorphism
$$
\gamma : \CH^*(X) \longrightarrow \bigoplus\nolimits_{i \geq 0} H^{2i}(X)(i)
$$
compatible with pullbacks such that $ch^H(\alpha) = \gamma(ch(\alpha))$
for $\alpha$ in $K_0(\textit{Vect}(X))$.

nodes.title: Divide pullback good blowing up
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIH}}


Let $b : X' \to X$ be the blowing up of a smooth projective
scheme over $k$ in a smooth closed subscheme $Z \subset X$.
Picture
$$
\begin{array}{cc}E \underset{j}{\longrightarrow}\underset{\pi}{\downarrow} & X' \overset{b}{\downarrow} \\ Z \overset{i}{\longrightarrow} & X\end{array}
$$
Assume there exists an element of $K_0(X)$ whose restriction to
$Z$ is equal to the class of $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ in $K_0(Z)$.
Assume every irreducible component of $Z$ has codimension $r$ in $X$.
Then there exists a cycle $\theta \in \CH^{r - 1}(X')$
such that $b^![Z] = [E] \cdot \theta$ in $\CH^r(X')$ and
$\pi_*j^!(\theta) = [Z]$ in $\CH^r(Z)$.

nodes.title: A5 A6 imply
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FII}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FII}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A4)
and (A7). Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $k$. Let $Z \subset X$
be a smooth closed subscheme such that every irreducible component of $Z$
has codimension $r$ in $X$. Assume the class of
$\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ in $K_0(Z)$ is the restriction of an element of $K_0(X)$.
If $a \in H^*(X)$ and $a|_Z = 0$ in $H^*(Z)$, then
$\gamma([Z]) \cup a = 0$.

nodes.title: Poincare duality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIJ}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A7).
Then axiom (A) of Section \ref{weil-section-axioms} holds with
$\int_X = \lambda$ as in axiom (A6).

nodes.title: Trace product
Trace base
Ok for projective bundle
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIN}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A7).
Let $p : P \to X$ be as in axiom (A3) with $X$ nonempty equidimensional.
Then $\gamma$ commutes with pushforward along $p$.

nodes.title: Integrate 1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FVR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FVR}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A7).
If $k'/k$ is a Galois extension, then we have
$\int_{\Spec(k')} 1 = [k' : k]$.

nodes.title: Enough
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIP}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A7).
In order to show that $\gamma$ commutes with pushforward it suffices
to show that $i_*(1) = \gamma([Z])$ if $i : Z \to X$ is a closed
immersion of nonempty smooth projective equidimensional schemes over $k$.

nodes.title: Grassmanian
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIQ}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A7).
Given integers $0 < l < n$ and a nonempty equidimensional
smooth projective scheme $X$ over $k$ consider the projection morphism
$p : X \times \mathbf{G}(l, n) \to X$.
Then $\gamma$ commutes with pushforward along $p$.

nodes.title: Enough better
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIR}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A7).
In order to show that $\gamma$ commutes with pushforward it suffices
to show that $i_*(1) = \gamma([Z])$ if $i : Z \to X$ is a closed
immersion of nonempty smooth projective equidimensional schemes over $k$
such that the class of $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ in $K_0(Z)$ is the
pullback of a class in $K_0(X)$.

nodes.title: Injective H0
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FVS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FVS}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A7).
If $k''/k'/k$ are finite separable field extensions, then
$H^0(\Spec(k')) \to H^0(\Spec(k''))$ is injective.

nodes.title: Pushforward blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FIS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FIS}}


Assume given data (D0), (D1), and (D2') satisfying axioms (A1) -- (A8).
Let $b : X' \to X$ be a blowing up of a smooth projective scheme $X$
over $k$ which is nonempty equidimensional of dimension $d$
in a nonwhere dense smooth center $Z$. Then $b_*(1) = 1$.

nodes.title: Done
Get weil
Check over extension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FVT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FVT}}


Let $k'/k$ be an extension of fields. Let $F'/F$ be an extension
of fields of characteristic $0$. Assume given
\begin{enumerate}
\item data (D0), (D1), (D2') for $k$ and $F$ denoted
$F(1), H^*, c_1^H$,
\item data (D0), (D1), (D2') for $k'$ and $F'$ denoted
$F'(1), (H')^*, c_1^{H'}$, and
\item an isomorphism $F(1) \otimes_F F' \to F'(1)$, functorial isomorphisms
$H^*(X) \otimes_F F' \to (H')^*(X_{k'})$ on the category of smooth projective
schemes $X$ over $k$ such that the diagrams
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\Pic(X) \underset{c_1^H}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow & H^2(X)(1) \downarrow \\ \Pic(X_{k'}) \overset{c_1^{H'}}{\longrightarrow} & (H')^2(X_{k'})(1)\end{array}
$$
commute.
\end{enumerate}
In this case, if $F'(1), (H')^*, c_1^{H'}$ satisfy axioms (A1) -- (A9),
then the same is true for $F(1), H^*, c_1^H$.

nodes.title: Base change de rham
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FL5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FL5}}


Let
$$
\begin{array}{cc}X' \underset{f}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow & X \downarrow \\ S' \longrightarrow & S\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of schemes. Then the maps discussed
above induce isomorphisms
$f^*\Omega^p_{X/S} \to \Omega^p_{X'/S'}$.

nodes.title: Etale
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FLV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FLV}}


Consider a commutative diagram of schemes
$$
\begin{array}{cc}X' \underset{f}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow & X \downarrow \\ S' \longrightarrow & S\end{array}
$$
If $X' \to X$ and $S' \to S$ are \'etale, then the maps discussed
above induce isomorphisms
$f^*\Omega^p_{X/S} \to \Omega^p_{X'/S'}$.

nodes.title: De rham affine
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FLW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FLW}}


Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of affine schemes given by the ring map
$R \to A$. Then $R\Gamma(X, \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}) = \Omega^\bullet_{A/R}$
in $D(R)$ and $H^i_{dR}(X/S) = H^i(\Omega^\bullet_{A/R})$.

nodes.title: Quasi coherence relative
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FLX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FLX}}


Let $p : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. If $p$ is quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, then $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is an object
of $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)$.

nodes.title: Coherence relative
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FLY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FLY}}


Let $p : X \to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes with $S$ locally
Noetherian. Then $Rp_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is an object
of $D_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_S)$.

nodes.title: Finite de Rham
Proper smooth de Rham
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FM0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FM0}}


Let $f : X \to S$ be a proper smooth morphism of schemes. Then
$Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}$, $p \geq 0$ and $Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ are
perfect objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_S)$ whose formation commutes
with arbitrary change of base.

nodes.title: Cup product graded commutative
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FM3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FM3}}


Let $p : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The cup product on $H^*_{dR}(X/S)$ is associative and
graded commutative.

nodes.title: Cup product hodge graded commutative
Hodge filtration
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FM8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FM8}}


Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. The {\it Hodge filtration}
on $H^n_{dR}(X/S)$ is the filtration with terms
$$
F^pH^n_{dR}(X/S) = \Im\left(H^n(X, \sigma_{\geq p}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S})
\longrightarrow H^n_{dR}(X/S)\right)
$$
where $\sigma_{\geq p}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ is as in
Homology, Section \ref{homology-section-truncations}.

nodes.title: De rham complex product
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMA}}


In the situation above there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\text{Tot}(\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \boxtimes \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S})
\longrightarrow
\Omega^\bullet_{X \times_S Y/S}
$$
of complexes of $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S$-modules.

nodes.title: Kunneth de rham
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMB}}


Assume $X$ and $Y$ are smooth, quasi-compact, with affine diagonal over
$S = \Spec(A)$. Then the map
$$
R\Gamma(X, \Omega^\bullet_{X/S})
\otimes_A^\mathbf{L}
R\Gamma(Y, \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S})
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma(X \times_S Y, \Omega^\bullet_{X \times_S Y/S})
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(A)$.

nodes.title: Kunneth de rham relative
Pullback c1
The complex for L star
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUF}}


With notation as above, there is a short exact sequence of complexes
$$
0 \to \Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to
\Omega^\bullet_{L^\star/S, 0} \to
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}[-1] \to 0
$$

nodes.title: The complex for L star gives chern class
Push omega a
Line bundle characteristic zero
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUI}}


In the situation above, assume there is a morphism $S \to \Spec(\mathbf{Q})$.
Then $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to \pi_*\Omega^\bullet_{L/S}$ is a
quasi-isomorphism and $H_{dR}^*(X/S) = H_{dR}^*(L/S)$.

nodes.title: Euler sequence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMH}}


There exists a short exact sequence
$$
0 \to \Omega \to \mathcal{O}(-1)^{\oplus n + 1} \to \mathcal{O} \to 0
$$

nodes.title: Twisted hodge cohomology projective space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUK}}


In the situation above we have the following cohomology groups
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^q(\mathbf{P}^n_A, \Omega^p) = 0$
unless $0 \leq p = q \leq n$,
\item for $0 \leq p \leq n$ the $A$-module
$H^p(\mathbf{P}^n_A, \Omega^p)$ free of rank $1$.
\item for $q > 0$, $k > 0$, and $p$ arbitrary we have
$H^q(\mathbf{P}^n_A, \Omega^p(k)) = 0$, and
\item add more here.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Hodge cohomology projective space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMI}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMI}}


We have $H^q(\mathbf{P}^n_A, \Omega^p) = 0$
unless $0 \leq p = q \leq n$. For $0 \leq p \leq n$ the $A$-module
$H^p(\mathbf{P}^n_A, \Omega^p)$ free of rank $1$ with basis element
$c_1^{Hodge}(\mathcal{O}(1))^p$.

nodes.title: De rham cohomology projective space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMJ}}


For $0 \leq i \leq n$ the de Rham cohomology
$H^{2i}_{dR}(\mathbf{P}^n_A/A)$ is a free $A$-module of rank $1$
with basis element $c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}(1))^i$.
In all other degrees the de Rham cohomology of $\mathbf{P}^n_A$
over $A$ is zero.

nodes.title: Spectral sequence smooth
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMM}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and smooth
morphism of schemes over a base scheme $S$. There is a bounded spectral
sequence with first page
$$
E_1^{p, q} =
H^q(\Omega^p_{Y/S} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L} Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/Y})
$$
converging to $R^{p + q}f_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$.

nodes.title: Relative global generation on fibres
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMP}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ be a smooth proper morphism of schemes.
Let $N$ and $n_1, \ldots, n_N \geq 0$ be integers and let
$\xi_i \in H^{n_i}_{dR}(X/Y)$, $1 \leq i \leq N$.
Assume for all points $y \in Y$ the images of $\xi_1, \ldots, \xi_N$
in $H^*_{dR}(X_y/y)$ form a basis over $\kappa(y)$. Then the map
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1}^N \mathcal{O}_Y[-n_i]
\longrightarrow
Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/Y}
$$
associated to $\xi_1, \ldots, \xi_N$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Global generation on fibres
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUM}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ be a smooth proper morphism of schemes over a base $S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ and $S$ are affine, and
\item there exist integers $N$ and $n_1, \ldots, n_N \geq 0$ and
$\xi_i \in H^{n_i}_{dR}(X/S)$, $1 \leq i \leq N$ such that
for all points $y \in Y$ the images of $\xi_1, \ldots, \xi_N$
in $H^*_{dR}(X_y/y)$ form a basis over $\kappa(y)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1}^N H^*_{dR}(Y/S) \longrightarrow
H^*_{dR}(X/S), \quad
(a_1, \ldots, a_N) \longmapsto  \sum \xi_i \cup f^*a_i
$$
is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Global generation on fibres
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMR}}


Let $f : X \to Y$ be a smooth proper morphism of schemes over a base $S$.
Let $N$ and $n_1, \ldots, n_N \geq 0$ be integers and let
$\xi_i \in H^{n_i}_{dR}(X/S)$, $1 \leq i \leq N$.
Assume for all points $y \in Y$ the images of $\xi_1, \ldots, \xi_N$
in $H^*_{dR}(X_y/y)$ form a basis over $\kappa(y)$. The map
$$
\tilde \xi = \bigoplus \tilde \xi_i[-n_i] :
\bigoplus \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}[-n_i]
\longrightarrow
Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}
$$
(see proof) is an isomorphism in $D(Y, (Y \to S)^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S)$ and
correspondingly the map
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1}^N H^*_{dR}(Y/S) \longrightarrow
H^*_{dR}(X/S), \quad
(a_1, \ldots, a_N) \longmapsto  \sum \xi_i \cup f^*a_i
$$
is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Projective space bundle formula
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMT}}


Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a locally
free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module of constant rank $r$. Consider the morphism
$p : P = \mathbf{P}(\mathcal{E}) \to X$.
Then the map
$$
\bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, r - 1} H^*_{dR}(X/S)
\longrightarrow
H^*_{dR}(P/S)
$$
given by the rule
$$
(a_0, \ldots, a_{r - 1}) \longmapsto
\sum\nolimits_{i = 0, \ldots, r - 1} c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}_P(1))^i \cup p^*(a_i)
$$
is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Local product
Log complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMW}}


Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $Y \subset X$ be an
effective Cartier divisor.
Assume the de Rham complex of log poles is defined for $Y \subset X$ over $S$.
There is a canonical short exact sequence
of complexes
$$
0 \to \Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}(\log Y) \to
\Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}[-1] \to 0
$$

nodes.title: Log complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUA}}



Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $Y \subset X$ be an
effective Cartier divisor. Assume the de Rham complex of log poles
is defined for $Y \subset X$ over $S$. Then the complex
$$
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}(\log Y)
$$
constructed in Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-log-complex} is the
{\it de Rham complex of log poles for $Y \subset X$ over $S$}.

nodes.title: Multiplication log
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUP}}


Let $p : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $Y \subset X$ be an
effective Cartier divisor. Assume the de Rham complex of log poles
is defined for $Y \subset X$ over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The maps
$\wedge : \Omega^p_{X/S} \times \Omega^q_{X/S} \to \Omega^{p + q}_{X/S}$
extend uniquely to $\mathcal{O}_X$-bilinear maps
$$
\wedge : \Omega^p_{X/S}(\log Y) \times \Omega^q_{X/S}(\log Y)
\to \Omega^{p + q}_{X/S}(\log Y)
$$
satisfying the Leibniz rule
$
\text{d}(\omega \wedge \eta) = \text{d}(\omega) \wedge \eta +
(-1)^{\deg(\omega)} \omega \wedge \text{d}(\eta)$,
\item with multiplication as in (1) the map
$\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}(\log(Y)$
is a homomorphism of differential graded $\mathcal{O}_S$-algebras,
\item via the maps in (1) we have $\Omega^p_{X/S}(\log Y) =
\wedge^p(\Omega^1_{X/S}(\log Y))$, and
\item the map
$\text{Res} : \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}(\log Y) \to \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}[-1]$
satisfies
$$
\text{Res}(\omega \wedge \eta) = \text{Res}(\omega) \wedge \eta|_Y
$$
for $\omega$ a local section of $\Omega^p_{X/S}(\log Y)$ and $\eta$
a local section of $\Omega^q_{X/S}$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Gysin via log complex
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUQ}}



Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $Y \subset X$ be an effective
Cartier divisor. Assume the de Rham complex of log poles is defined for
$Y \subset X$ over $S$. Denote
$$
\delta : \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S} \to \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}[2]
$$
in $D(X, f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S)$ the ``boundary'' map coming from the
short exact sequence in Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-log-complex}. Denote
$$
\xi' : \Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}[2]
$$
in $D(X, f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S)$ the map of
Remark \ref{derham-remark-cup-product-as-a-map}
corresponding to $\xi = c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}_X(-Y))$. Denote
$$
\zeta' : \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S} \to \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}[2]
$$
in $D(Y, f|_Y^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S)$ the map of
Remark \ref{derham-remark-cup-product-as-a-map} corresponding to
$\zeta = c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}_X(-Y)|_Y)$. Then the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \underset{\xi'}{\downarrow}\longrightarrow & \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S} \overset{\zeta'}{\downarrow}\underset{\delta}{\swarrow} \\ \Omega^\bullet_{X/S}[2] \longrightarrow & \Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}[2]\end{array}
$$
is commutative in $D(X, f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S)$.

nodes.title: Log complex consequence
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMX}}


Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $Y \subset X$ be an effective
Cartier divisor. Assume the de Rham complex of log poles is defined for
$Y \subset X$ over $S$. Let $b \in H^m_{dR}(X/S)$ be a de Rham cohomology
class whose restriction to $Y$ is zero. Then
$c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{O}_X(Y)) \cup b = 0$ in $H^{m + 2}_{dR}(X/S)$.

nodes.title: Check log smooth
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FMY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FMY}}


Let $X \to T \to S$ be morphisms of schemes. Let $Y \subset X$ be an effective
Cartier divisor. If both $X \to T$ and $Y \to T$ are smooth, then
the de Rham complex of log poles is defined for $Y \subset X$ over $S$.

nodes.title: Comparison
Comparison bis
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G5G}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G5G}}


For $a \geq 0$ there are canonical maps
$$
b^*\Omega^a_{X/S} \longrightarrow
\Omega^a_{L/S} \longrightarrow
b^*\Omega^a_{X/S} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_L} \mathcal{O}_L((n - 1)E)
$$
whose composition is induced by the inclusion
$\mathcal{O}_L \subset \mathcal{O}_L((n - 1)E)$.

nodes.title: Blowup twist same cohomology
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G5H}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G5H}}


Let $E = 0(P)$ be the exceptional divisor of the blowing up $b$.
For any locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{E}$ and
$0 \leq i \leq n - 1$ the map
$$
\mathcal{E}
\longrightarrow
Rb_*(b^*\mathcal{E} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_L} \mathcal{O}_L(iE))
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

nodes.title: Comparison general
Distinguished triangle blowup
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FUV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FUV}}


With notation as in More on Morphisms, Lemma \ref{more-morphisms-lemma-blowup}
and denoting $f : X \to S$ the structure morphism there is a canonical
distinguished triangle
$$
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to
Rb_*(\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S}) \oplus i_*\Omega^\bullet_{Z/S} \to
i_*Rp_*(\Omega^\bullet_{E/S}) \to
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}[1]
$$
in $D(X, f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_S)$ where the four maps
$$
\begin{matrix}
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} & \to & Rb_*(\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S}), \\
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} & \to & i_*\Omega^\bullet_{Z/S}, \\
Rb_*(\Omega^\bullet_{X'/S}) & \to & i_*Rp_*(\Omega^\bullet_{E/S}), \\
i_*\Omega^\bullet_{Z/S} & \to & i_*Rp_*(\Omega^\bullet_{E/S})
\end{matrix}
$$
are the canonical ones (Section \ref{derham-section-de-rham-complex}),
except with sign reversed for one of them.

nodes.title: Blowup split
Ext zero
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G5I}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G5I}}


Let $i : Z \to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes which is regular of
codimension $c$. Then $\Ext^q_{\mathcal{O}_X}(i_*\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}) = 0$
for $q < c$ for $\mathcal{E}$ locally free on $X$ and $\mathcal{F}$
any $\mathcal{O}_Z$-module.

nodes.title: Splitting on omega a
Funny map
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FL8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FL8}}


Let $R$ be a ring and consider a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}0 \longrightarrow & K^0 \longrightarrow & L^0 \longrightarrow & M^0 \longrightarrow & 0 \\  &  & L^{-1} \underset{\partial}{\uparrow}\xlongequal{} & M^{-1} \uparrow & \end{array}
$$
of $R$-modules with exact top row and $M^0$ and $M^{-1}$
finite free of the same rank. For $p \geq 0$ there are canonical maps
$$
c^p :
\wedge^p(H^0(L^\bullet))
\longrightarrow
\wedge^p(K^0) \otimes_R \det(M^\bullet)
$$
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $c^0(1) = \delta(M^\bullet)$, and
\item $c^{q + p}(\omega \wedge \eta) = \omega \wedge c^p(\eta)$
for $\omega \in \wedge^q(K^0)$ and $\eta \in \wedge^p(H^0(L^\bullet))$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the composition of $c^p$ with the map
$\wedge^p(K^0) \to \wedge^p(H^0(L^\bullet))$ is multiplication
with $\delta(M^\bullet)$.

nodes.title: Funny map functorial
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H9F}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H9F}}



Let $R_1 \to R_2$ be a ring homomorphism. For $i = 1, 2$ consider
commutative diagrams
$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}0 \longrightarrow & K_i^0 \longrightarrow & L_i^0 \longrightarrow & M_i^0 \longrightarrow & 0 \\  &  & L_i^{-1} \underset{\partial_i}{\uparrow}\xlongequal{} & M_i^{-1} \uparrow & \end{array}
$$
of $R_i$-modules as in Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-funny-map}. Assume we have
maps $K_1^0 \to K_2^0$, $L_1^j \to L_2^j$, $M_1^j \to M_2^j$
compatible with the given ring map $R_1 \to R_2$ and
compatible with the maps in the displayed diagrams. If the maps
$M_1^j \otimes_{R_1} R_2 \to M_2^j$ are isomorphisms, then
the diagrams
$$
\begin{array}{cc}\wedge^p(H^0(L_1^\bullet)) \downarrow\underset{c^p}{\longrightarrow} & \wedge^p(K_1^0) \otimes_{R_1} \det(M_1^\bullet) \downarrow \\ \wedge^p(H^0(L_2^\bullet))
\overset{c^p}{\longrightarrow} & \wedge^p(K_2^0) \otimes_{R_2} \det(M_2^\bullet)\end{array}
$$
commute.

nodes.title: Base change Garel upstairs
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H9G}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H9G}}


Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}Y' \underset{f'}{\downarrow}\underset{b}{\longrightarrow} & Y \overset{f}{\downarrow} \\ X' \overset{a}{\longrightarrow} & X\end{array}
$$
of schemes which induces an isomorphism of $Y'$ with an open subscheme of
$X' \times_X Y$. Assume $f$ is locally quasi-finite and syntomic and
assume given maps $c^p_{Y/X} : \Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}} \to
f^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \det(\NL_{Y/X})$
for $p \geq 0$ satisfying
(\ref{item-degree-zero}) and (\ref{item-multiplicative}).
Then there is at most one collection of maps
$c^p_{Y'/X'} : \Omega^p_{Y'/\mathbf{Z}} \to
(f')^*\Omega^p_{X'/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y'}} \det(\NL_{Y'/X'})$
for $p \geq 0$
satisfying (\ref{item-degree-zero}) and (\ref{item-multiplicative})
such that the diagrams
$$
\begin{array}{cccc}b^*\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}} \underset{b^*c^p_{Y/X}}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow &  & b^*(f^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \det(\NL_{Y/X}))
\xlongequal{} & (f')^*a^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} b^*\det(\NL_{Y/X}))
\downarrow \\ \Omega^p_{Y'/\mathbf{Z}} \overset{c^p_{Y'/X'}}{\longrightarrow} &  &  & (f')^*\Omega^p_{X'/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y'}} \det(\NL_{Y'/X'})\end{array}
$$
commute for all $p \geq 0$. Here the vertical arrows use the maps
$b^*\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}} \to \Omega^p_{Y'/\mathbf{Z}}$ and
$a^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \to \Omega^p_{X'/\mathbf{Z}}$
of Section \ref{derham-section-de-rham-complex}
as well as the identification $b^*\det(\NL_{Y/X}) = \det(\NL_{Y'/X'})$ of
Discriminants, Section \ref{discriminant-section-tate-map}.

nodes.title: Existence base change Garel upstairs
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H9H}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0H9H}}



Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}Y' \underset{f'}{\downarrow}\underset{b}{\longrightarrow} & Y \overset{f}{\downarrow} \\ X' \overset{a}{\longrightarrow} & X\end{array}
$$
of schemes which induces an isomorphism of $Y'$ with an open subscheme of
$X' \times_X Y$. Assume $f$ is locally quasi-finite and syntomic. Then for
every $y' \in Y'$ we can find opens $V' \subset Y'$,
$V \subset Y$, $U' \subset X$, $U \subset X$ with $y' \in V'$, with
$f'(V') \subset U'$, $b(V') \subset V$, $a(U') \subset U$,
$f(V) \subset U$, and such that for $p \geq 0$ there are maps
$c^p_{V/U}$ and $c^p_{V'/U'}$ satisfying (\ref{item-degree-zero})
and (\ref{item-multiplicative}) which are compatible with the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}V' \downarrow\underset{b}{\longrightarrow} & V \downarrow \\ U' \longrightarrow & U\end{array}
$$
in the sense explained in Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-base-change-Garel-upstairs}.

nodes.title: Garel upstairs
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FLA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FLA}}


There exists a unique rule that to every locally quasi-finite syntomic
morphism of schemes $f : Y \to X$ assigns $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module maps
$$
c^p_{Y/X} :
\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}}
\longrightarrow
f^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \det(\NL_{Y/X})
$$
for $p \geq 0$ satisfying (\ref{item-degree-zero}), (\ref{item-multiplicative}),
and (\ref{item-base-change}). In particular, the composition of
$c^p_{Y/X}$ with $f^*\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \to \Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}}$
is multiplication by $\delta(\NL_{Y/X})$.

nodes.title: Garel
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FLB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FLB}}


There exists a unique rule that to every finite syntomic
morphism of schemes $f : Y \to X$ assigns $\mathcal{O}_X$-module maps
$$
\Theta^p_{Y/X} :
f_*\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}}
\longrightarrow
\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}}
$$
satisfying the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item the composition with
$\Omega^p_{X/\mathbf{Z}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} f_*\mathcal{O}_Y
\to f_*\Omega^p_{Y/\mathbf{Z}}$ is equal to
$\text{id} \otimes \text{Trace}_f$
where $\text{Trace}_f : f_*\mathcal{O}_Y \to \mathcal{O}_X$
is the map from
Discriminants, Section \ref{discriminant-section-discriminant},
\item the rule is compatible with base change.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Garel
Garel map frobenius smooth char p
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FW2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FW2}}


Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $X \to S$ be a smooth morphism
of relative dimension $d$ of schemes in characteristic $p$.
The relative Frobenius $F_{X/S} : X \to X^{(p)}$ of $X/S$
(Varieties, Definition \ref{varieties-definition-relative-frobenius})
is finite syntomic and the corresponding map
$$
\Theta_{X/X^{(p)}} :
F_{X/S, *}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \to \Omega^\bullet_{X^{(p)}/S}
$$
is zero in all degrees except in degree $d$ where it defines a
surjection.

nodes.title: Duality hodge
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FW4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FW4}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth proper scheme over $k$
equidimensional of dimension $d$. There exists a $k$-linear map
$$
t : H^d(X, \Omega^d_{X/k}) \longrightarrow k
$$
unique up to precomposing by multiplication by a unit of
$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ with the following property: for all $p, q$ the pairing
$$
H^q(X, \Omega^p_{X/k}) \times H^{d - q}(X, \Omega^{d - p}_{X/k})
\longrightarrow
k, \quad
(\xi, \xi') \longmapsto t(\xi \cup \xi')
$$
is perfect.

nodes.title: Bottom part degenerates
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FW5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FW5}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a smooth proper scheme over $k$. The map
$$
\text{d} : H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to H^0(X, \Omega^1_{X/k})
$$
is zero.

nodes.title: Top part degenerates
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FW6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FW6}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a smooth proper scheme over $k$
equidimensional of dimension $d$. The map
$$
\text{d} : H^d(X, \Omega^{d - 1}_{X/k}) \to H^d(X, \Omega^d_{X/k})
$$
is zero.

nodes.title: Poincare duality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FW7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FW7}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth proper scheme over $k$
equidimensional of dimension $d$. There exists a $k$-linear map
$$
t : H^{2d}_{dR}(X/k) \longrightarrow k
$$
unique up to precomposing by multiplication by a unit of
$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ with the following property: for all $i$ the pairing
$$
H^i_{dR}(X/k) \times H_{dR}^{2d - i}(X/k)
\longrightarrow
k, \quad
(\xi, \xi') \longmapsto t(\xi \cup \xi')
$$
is perfect.

nodes.title: Chern classes
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FW9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FW9}}


There is a unique rule which assigns to every quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme $X$ a total Chern class
$$
c^{dR} :
K_0(\textit{Vect}(X))
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \geq 0} H^{2i}_{dR}(X/\mathbf{Z})
$$
with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item we have $c^{dR}(\alpha + \beta) = c^{dR}(\alpha) c^{dR}(\beta)$
for $\alpha, \beta \in K_0(\textit{Vect}(X))$,
\item if $f : X \to X'$ is a morphism of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes, then $c^{dR}(f^*\alpha) = f^*c^{dR}(\alpha)$,
\item given $\mathcal{L} \in \Pic(X)$ we have
$c^{dR}([\mathcal{L}]) = 1 + c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{L})$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Chern character
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FWB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FWB}}


There is a unique rule which assigns to every quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme $X$ over $\mathbf{Q}$ a ``chern character''
$$
ch^{dR} : K_0(\textit{Vect}(X)) \longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \geq 0} H_{dR}^{2i}(X/\mathbf{Q})
$$
with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $ch^{dR}$ is a ring map for all $X$,
\item if $f : X' \to X$ is a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes over $\mathbf{Q}$, then $f^* \circ ch^{dR} =  ch^{dR} \circ f^*$, and
\item given $\mathcal{L} \in \Pic(X)$
we have $ch^{dR}([\mathcal{L}]) = \exp(c_1^{dR}(\mathcal{L}))$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: De rham is weil
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FWD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0FWD}}


Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero. The functor that
sends a smooth projective scheme $X$ over $k$ to $H_{dR}^*(X/k)$
is a Weil cohomology theory in the sense of
Weil Cohomology Theories, Definition
\ref{weil-definition-weil-cohomology-theory}.

nodes.title: Gysin differential
Gysin global
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G86}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G86}}



Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $Z \to X$ be a closed immersion
of finite presentation whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ is
locally free of rank $c$. Then there is a canonical map
$$
\gamma^p : \Omega^p_{Z/S} \to \mathcal{H}^c_Z(\Omega^{p + c}_{X/S})
$$
which is locally given by the maps $\gamma^p_{f_1, \ldots, f_c}$
of Remark \ref{derham-remark-gysin-equations}.

nodes.title: Gysin differential global
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G87}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G87}}



Let $X \to S$ and $i : Z \to X$ be as in Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-gysin-global}.
The Gysin map $\gamma^p$ is compatible with the de Rham
differentials on $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^\bullet_{Z/S}$.

nodes.title: Gysin projection
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G88}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G88}}



Let $X \to S$ and $i : Z \to X$ be as in Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-gysin-global}.
Given $\alpha \in H^q(X, \Omega^p_{X/S})$ we have
$\gamma^p(\alpha|_Z) = i^{-1}\alpha \wedge \gamma^0(1)$ in
$H^q(Z, \mathcal{H}^c_Z(\Omega^{p + c}_{X/S}))$.
Please see proof for notation.

nodes.title: Gysin transverse
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G89}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G89}}



Let $c \geq 0$ be an integer. Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}Z' \underset{h}{\downarrow}\longrightarrow & X' \underset{g}{\downarrow}\longrightarrow & S' \downarrow \\ Z \longrightarrow & X \longrightarrow & S\end{array}
$$
be a commutative diagram of schemes.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z \to X$ and $Z' \to X'$
satisfy the assumptions of Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-gysin-global},
\item the left square in the diagram is cartesian, and
\item $h^*\mathcal{C}_{Z/X} \to \mathcal{C}_{Z'/X'}$
(Morphisms, Lemma \ref{morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial})
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}h^*\Omega^p_{Z/S} \underset{h^{-1}\gamma^p}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow &  & \mathcal{O}_{X'}|_{Z'} \otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal{O}_X|_Z}
h^{-1}\mathcal{H}^c_Z(\Omega^{p + c}_{X/S}) \downarrow \\ \Omega^p_{Z'/S'} \overset{\gamma^p}{\longrightarrow} &  & \mathcal{H}^c_{Z'}(\Omega^{p + c}_{X'/S'})\end{array}
$$
is commutative. The left vertical arrow is functoriality of modules of
differentials and the right vertical arrow uses
Cohomology, Remark \ref{cohomology-remark-support-functorial}.

nodes.title: Gysin differential hodge
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8B}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8B}}



Let $X \to S$ and $i : Z \to X$ be as in Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-gysin-global}.
Assume $X \to S$ is smooth and $Z \to X$ Koszul regular.
The Gysin maps $\gamma^{p, q}$ are compatible with the de Rham
differentials on $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^\bullet_{Z/S}$.

nodes.title: Gysin projection global
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8C}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8C}}



Let $X \to S$, $i : Z \to X$, and $c \geq 0$ be as in
Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-gysin-global}. Assume $X \to S$ smooth and
$Z \to X$ Koszul regular. Given $\alpha \in H^q(X, \Omega^p_{X/S})$ we have
$\gamma^{p, q}(\alpha|_Z) = \alpha \cup \gamma^{0, 0}(1)$ in
$H^{q + c}(X, \Omega^{p + c}_{X/S})$ with $\gamma^{a, b}$ as in
Remark \ref{derham-remark-how-to-use}.

nodes.title: Gysin transverse global
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8D}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8D}}



Let $c \geq 0$ and
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}Z' \underset{h}{\downarrow}\longrightarrow & X' \underset{g}{\downarrow}\longrightarrow & S' \downarrow \\ Z \longrightarrow & X \longrightarrow & S\end{array}
$$
satisfy the assumptions of Lemma \ref{derham-lemma-gysin-transverse} and assume
in addition that $X \to S$ and $X' \to S'$ are smooth and that
$Z \to X$ and $Z' \to X'$ are Koszul regular immersions.
Then the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}H^q(Z, \Omega^p_{Z/S}) \underset{\gamma^{p, q}}{\longrightarrow}\downarrow &  & H^{q + c}(X, \Omega^{p + c}_{X/S}) \downarrow \\ H^q(Z', \Omega^p_{Z'/S'}) \overset{\gamma^{p, q}}{\longrightarrow} &  & H^{q + c}(X', \Omega^{p + c}_{X'/S'})\end{array}
$$
is commutative where $\gamma^{p, q}$ is as in Remark \ref{derham-remark-how-to-use}.

nodes.title: Class of a point
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8E}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8E}}



Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an irreducible smooth proper scheme over $k$
of dimension $d$. Let $Z \subset X$ be the reduced closed subscheme consisting
of a single $k$-rational point $x$. Then the image of
$1 \in k = H^0(Z, \mathcal{O}_Z) = H^0(Z, \Omega^0_{Z/k})$
by the map $H^0(Z, \Omega^0_{Z/k}) \to H^d(X, \Omega^d_{X/k})$
of Remark \ref{derham-remark-how-to-use} is nonzero.

nodes.title: Situation: Relative duality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8G}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8G}}


Here $S$ is a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and
$f : X \to S$ is a proper smooth morphism of schemes all of whose
fibres are nonempty and equidimensional of dimension $n$.

nodes.title: Relative bottom part degenerates
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8H}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8H}}



In Situation \ref{derham-situation-relative-duality} the pushforward
$f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a finite \'etale $\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra
and locally on $S$ we have $Rf_*\mathcal{O}_X = f_*\mathcal{O}_X \oplus P$
in $D(\mathcal{O}_S)$ with $P$ perfect of tor amplitude in $[1, \infty)$.
The map $\text{d} : f_*\mathcal{O}_X \to f_*\Omega_{X/S}$ is zero.

nodes.title: Relative duality hodge
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8I}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8I}}



In Situation \ref{derham-situation-relative-duality} there exists an
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module map
$$
t : Rf_*\Omega^n_{X/S}[n] \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_S
$$
unique up to precomposing by multiplication by a unit of
$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ with the following property: for all $p$ the pairing
$$
Rf_*\Omega^p_{X/S}
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S}^\mathbf{L}
Rf_*\Omega^{n - p}_{X/S}[n]
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{O}_S
$$
given by the relative cup product composed with $t$
is a perfect pairing of perfect complexes on $S$.

nodes.title: Relative top part degenerates
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8J}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8J}}



In Situation \ref{derham-situation-relative-duality} the map
$\text{d} : R^nf_*\Omega^{n - 1}_{X/S} \to R^nf_*\Omega^n_{X/S}$
is zero.

nodes.title: Relative poincare duality
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0G8K}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0G8K}}


Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $f : X \to S$
be a proper smooth morphism of schemes all of whose fibres are nonempty
and equidimensional of dimension $n$. There exists an
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module map
$$
t : R^{2n}f_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S} \longrightarrow \mathcal{O}_S
$$
unique up to precomposing by multiplication by a unit of
$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ with the following property: the pairing
$$
Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S}^\mathbf{L}
Rf_*\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}[2n]
\longrightarrow
\mathcal{O}_S, \quad
(\xi, \xi') \longmapsto t(\xi \cup \xi')
$$
is a perfect pairing of perfect complexes on $S$.
